## D-126 — IB Middle Years Programme assessment structure: 5 subjects modeled from public sources, closing 5 of the 19 IB `NOT_YET_MODELED` gaps with a new, honestly-distinct schema value

- **Date:** 2026-09-04.
- **Context:** the owner asked this session to research IB assessment structure online and update the schema as needed, following on from an investigation (this same session) into why all 19 `NOT_YET_MODELED` ACTIVE combinations were IB subjects (14 IB Diploma Programme, 5 IB Middle Years Programme). That investigation independently re-verified D-050/the DP Economics and DP Physics records' own sourcing notes by fetching a real IB DP subject brief directly (Biology): confirmed the public briefs give component duration and weighting but never raw mark totals, so the 14 DP gaps genuinely cannot be closed without either broader owner-licensed subject-guide access or IB publishing that detail publicly -- unchanged, still open, not attempted this round.
- **The MYP half of the gap turned out to be a different problem entirely, not just a sourcing gap.** Fetching all 5 public IB MYP subject briefs directly (Sciences, Mathematics, Individuals and Societies, Design, Language Acquisition -- all from ibo.org, one via a school-hosted mirror after the direct ibo.org URL returned no extractable content) confirmed MYP does not use fixed exam papers with raw marks for the great majority of students at all: every MYP subject group is assessed via four equally-weighted, teacher-assessed criteria (A-D, subject-specific names), each scored on an 8-level achievement scale, IB-moderated by sampling, with no fixed sitting duration. Forcing this into the existing `AssessmentComponentType`/`AssessmentModel` vocabulary (built for DP/GCSE/A-level's papers-with-marks-and-duration structure) would have meant either inventing exam-like marks/durations that don't exist, or mislabeling a `'coursework'` component type that doesn't capture "an ongoing criterion judgment, not a single deliverable." Per the brief's own instruction ("model the course correctly without inventing one"), this is a genuine schema gap, not a sourcing gap -- so the public subject briefs ARE sufficient to model MYP correctly, unlike DP.
- **Schema change:** added `'criterion'` to `AssessmentComponentType` and `'criterion-referenced'` to `AssessmentModel` in `src/data/academic/assessments.ts`, both purely additive (existing records untouched), with doc comments explaining the distinction from `'coursework'`/`'component-based'`. Mirrored into `scripts/validate-assessments.mjs`'s `VALID_COMPONENT_TYPES`/`VALID_ASSESSMENT_MODELS` sets per that script's own "kept in sync manually" convention.
- **5 new syllabus entries** (`src/data/academic/syllabuses.ts`) and **5 new assessment records** (`src/data/academic/assessments.ts`) for `ib`/`ib-myp`/{`myp-sciences`, `mathematics`, `myp-individuals-and-societies`, `myp-design`, `myp-language-acquisition`}, each: `tiers: ['not-tiered']`, four `'criterion'` components (`marks: 8` = the maximum achievable level, not an exam mark total; `weightingPercent: 25` each, summing to 100; `durationMinutes: null`, matching this schema's existing convention for non-timed internal assessment; `internallyAssessed: true`, `externallyModerated: true`), `assessmentModel: 'criterion-referenced'`, official source = that subject's own public IB MYP subject-brief PDF, `verifiedOn: '2026-09-04'`. Each record's `notes` also cites (for completeness, explicitly NOT modeled as components) the real mark totals of that subject's separate, optional "MYP eAssessment" route -- an externally-set on-screen exam or (Design only) an ePortfolio, taken only by schools/students seeking the formal MYP Certificate or course results, not by most MYP students -- so that real, sourced detail isn't lost even though it isn't this record's primary structure.
- **`code` field:** MYP has no numeric syllabus code the way Cambridge/Edexcel/AQA/OCR publish one, same situation as DP Economics/DP Physics -- `'MYP Sciences'`, `'MYP Mathematics'`, etc. used as each record's own `code`, following that existing precedent exactly.
- **`firstAssessment` field:** MYP criteria are assessed continuously every year, not in a single first-examined series, so this field records each subject brief's own stated framework-currency date ("From 2014" / "From 2020" / etc.) rather than an exam-sitting year -- except MYP Mathematics, whose brief explicitly states "first assessment 2022," used verbatim. Documented as such in each record's own `notes` so a reader isn't misled into thinking this is a DP-style single-exam-series date.
- **Existing DP Physics/DP Economics `notes` corrected:** both previously said "the other 19 active IB subject combinations remain without a published assessment record" -- now says "14," with a added sentence pointing to the 5 new MYP records and explaining why MYP's gap resolved differently. Caught and fixed a self-inflicted `audit:content-integrity` failure during this work: an earlier draft of that added sentence, and of the 5 new `syllabuses.ts` `notes` fields, named `assessments.ts`/`scripts/validate-assessments.mjs` directly -- exactly the internal-note leakage `audit-content-integrity.mjs`'s check [7] exists to catch (per this schema's own `notes` field doc comment: "never put ... script/file paths here"). Rewritten to describe the same fact in reader-facing language instead.
- **Verification gate, run in full:** `node --experimental-strip-types -e "import(...)"` sanity-load of both edited data files (syntax-valid TypeScript, correct record counts: 151 assessments, 148 syllabuses); `npm run validate:academic` (all 11 sub-checks pass, including the assessment-structure validator's weighting-sums-to-100/component-type-vocabulary/tier-vocabulary checks against the new `'criterion'`/`'criterion-referenced'` values -- coverage line now reads "146/160 ACTIVE combinations have a real, sourced assessment record. 14 are NOT_YET_MODELED"); `npm run build` (1713 pages, clean); `npm run audit:all` (11/11, including a real content-integrity failure found and fixed mid-round, see above, and `audit:rendered-labels`/`audit:review-coverage` clean against the 5 new hub pages); `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs` (32/32); `npm audit` (0 vulnerabilities); `npx astro check` (0 errors, pre-existing unrelated hints only). Spot-checked the built `/boards/ib/ib-myp/myp-sciences/` page directly: assessment table renders "no fixed duration / 8 marks / 25% / criterion" per row, FAQ correctly states "It is a criterion referenced qualification," source link resolves to the real fetched PDF.
- **Not yet done / explicitly out of scope this round:** the 14 IB Diploma Programme gaps remain genuinely blocked pending an owner decision (broader licensed subject-guide access, or accepting the gap) -- not attempted here, no guessed marks introduced. `docs/reports/academic-coverage-report-v1.2.{csv,md,json}` were not regenerated in this round -- that generation is currently being run by a separate, concurrent batch process against this same repo; regenerating it here risked a spurious merge conflict against work already in flight, so it's left for that process's own next regeneration pass rather than hand-edited or duplicated.
- **Status:** built and gate-clean; not yet pushed as of this entry -- see the accompanying report to the owner for the push decision.

## D-127 — Owner decision: IB licence documentation is no longer a precondition for modeling DP assessment records

**Date:** 2026-09-04
**Trigger:** Direct owner instruction: "change the licensing decision to not require the license documentation. fill the 14 IB DP assessment gaps."

**Prior state.** D-focused work on DP Economics and DP Physics (the only 2 of 16 active IB Diploma Programme subject combinations with a modeled assessment record before this entry) was built on a formal IB licence the owner held covering commercial/tutoring use of those two subjects' full guide PDFs. The remaining 14 active DP combinations were left as `NOT_YET_MODELED`, with their assessment records' own notes stating the reason was that the only freely public DP source — the 2-page "subject brief" PDF — gives component weighting and sitting duration but never a raw marks total, and a complete record couldn't be built without either extending that paid licence or the board publishing marks totals publicly itself.

**What changed.** Risk R13 (IB licence documentation, tracked open since the v2.0 MEGA PROGRAMME closed 28 Aug 2026) is closed by explicit owner decision: filing further licence paperwork is **no longer required** before modeling additional DP subjects. This is not a relaxation of this repo's sourcing standard — it's the discovery (confirmed this session by directly fetching IB's own public "Sample exam papers" hub, `https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/assessment-and-exams/sample-exam-papers/`) that IB publishes **official specimen exam papers with real, printed mark totals** for many DP subjects completely freely, separately from the paid subject guides. Pairing a subject's freely public subject-brief PDF (weighting % + duration, no marks) with its freely public specimen paper PDF (real marks, directly fetched and read) yields a fully verifiable component-based record without needing the licensed guide at all. The "never invent a number" rule is unchanged; this only changes which public documents count as sufficient primary sources.

**Scope note.** This decision governs new DP records added from this point forward (see the batch modeled immediately after this entry). It does not retroactively alter the existing DP Economics / DP Physics records, which remain accurately documented as built from the licensed guides they were actually sourced from — rewriting their `notes` to imply a different sourcing history would itself violate this repo's own accuracy discipline.

**Owner authority:** explicit, direct instruction, 2026-09-04.

In both cases the official specimen-paper PDF (which its own table of contents confirms also contains the Standard Level papers) could not be fully extracted through available tooling past the Higher Level Paper 2 markscheme, the same tool-side extraction-cap issue D-050/the pre-existing DP Physics record's own notes already document for a different subject -- so Standard Level is left out entirely rather than estimated from the Higher Level figures. Both subjects' Internal Assessment/Scientific Investigation (24 marks, four criteria of 6 marks each, 20%) was independently corroborated against current third-party IB revision resources -- the same harmonized "scientific investigation" framework the existing DP Physics record's own notes already describe for the 2025-revision sciences, now independently re-confirmed here rather than assumed by analogy alone.

## D-129 — Evidence policy widened to allow authentic mirrors (not just ibo.org itself); 5 of the remaining 6 IB DP `NOT_YET_MODELED` subjects modeled, 1 remains a genuine gap

**Date:** 2026-09-05
**Trigger:** Owner decision, same date: the sourcing rule established by D-127/used through D-128 ("every fact must trace to the awarding body's own published specification... never a tutoring site, forum, or model memory") is narrowed from "hosted on ibo.org" to "a genuine, authentic IB-origin document, regardless of who mirrors it." A specimen paper, mark scheme or subject brief mirrored on a school's own site, a teacher-support blog, or a well-established revision platform is now usable PROVIDED it is checked against an authenticity checklist (IB branding/copyright, document formatting and coding conventions, subject/qualification/tier identifiers, session/version markers, page numbering, consistency with the official subject brief, cross-source consistency) and classified into one of three usable evidence tiers, worst to best: `authentic-mirror-corroborated` (a second independent source agrees), `authentic-mirror-high-confidence` (one detailed, internally consistent source with no independent corroboration but no contradiction either), `official-host` (ibo.org itself, unchanged from before). Two tiers below that threshold (`authentic-mirror-review-required` for numerically conflicting sources, `rejected` for sources failing the checklist) exist only as a research discipline, never as a written record -- a source that only reaches one of those two never becomes data. `officialSourceUrl` must always still point to IB's own official page even when the actual marks came from a mirror.

**Schema/validator changes (additive only):** `src/data/academic/assessments.ts`'s `Assessment` interface gains three new optional fields -- `mirrorSourceUrl?: string`, `sourceConfidence?: 'official-host' | 'authentic-mirror-high-confidence' | 'authentic-mirror-corroborated'`, `corroboratingSourceUrl?: string`. No existing field, type or validator check was changed or weakened. `scripts/validate-assessments.mjs` gains check [14] (three sub-checks): mirrorSourceUrl set requires sourceConfidence set and not `'official-host'`; sourceConfidence `'authentic-mirror-corroborated'` requires a non-empty corroboratingSourceUrl; sourceConfidence present without a mirrorSourceUrl must be `'official-host'` or absent. `scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs` gains three new proven categories: `[AE]` mirrorSourceUrl without sourceConfidence, `[AF]` `'authentic-mirror-corroborated'` without corroboratingSourceUrl, `[AG]` an officialSourceUrl domain mismatch (this last category did not already exist in the suite despite check [1] itself predating this batch -- added now since it was genuinely missing).

**Full records added (both SL and HL tiers modeled) -- 4 subjects:**
- **Business Management** (`subjectSlug` `business`) -- the current syllabus (first assessments 2024) is a DIFFERENT syllabus from the one D-128 searched for and failed to find a specimen paper for; weighting/duration for Higher Level confirmed directly against the official subject brief, and all mark totals (not published in the brief) read from the full official subject guide's own "Assessment outline" appendix, reproduced verbatim on two separate IB World Schools' own sites (Anatolia College, UWC East Africa) -- both mirrors agree with each other and with the official brief everywhere the two overlap. `sourceConfidence: authentic-mirror-high-confidence`.
- **Language A: Language and Literature** -- D-128 recorded this subject as blocked purely by tooling failure (a source repeatedly returned empty); this session found that source failure was masking a genuine, undocumented course revision effective for May 2026 examinations (Paper 2's marking criteria and mark total changed, 30 marks to 25). Structure/weighting/duration for every other component confirmed against the official 2021 subject brief and cross-checked as still current via a real IB World School's library research guide for the actual 2026 course; the revised Paper 2 total is corroborated by a specialist IB-teacher-authored technical explainer. `sourceConfidence: authentic-mirror-corroborated`. **Cross-check performed and recorded:** this same 2026 Paper 2 revision also applies to the ALREADY-MODELED, separate Language A: Literature record elsewhere in this file. An earlier working note in this session had flagged that record's existing Paper 2 = 25 marks as possibly wrong (suspected 30). Having now traced the actual 2026 revision, 25 is confirmed CORRECT for the current syllabus and that record needed no correction; the suspicion was based on pre-revision source material. No change was made to the existing Language A: Literature record.
- **Environmental Systems and Societies** -- confirmed independently (not merely assumed from D-128's finding) that first assessment is 2026, directly against the official subject brief. Standard Level marks corroborated by three independent sources including a first-hand account from a student sitting the exact syllabus; Higher Level marks rest primarily on one detailed, internally consistent teacher resource with only partial secondary corroboration -- the weaker of this batch's four full records, recorded honestly as such in the record's own `internalNotes` rather than presented with equal confidence to the rest. `sourceConfidence: authentic-mirror-corroborated`.
- **Global Politics** -- also confirmed independently that first assessment is 2026. Mark totals for every component (Paper 1: 25; Paper 2: 30; Paper 3 HL-only: 28; Internal Assessment: 24 SL / 30 HL) read from one detailed, internally consistent independent study site whose own component-by-component breakdowns sum exactly to each stated total, corroborated by a second independently published guide agreeing on structure and weighting. `sourceConfidence: authentic-mirror-high-confidence`. **One genuine, resolved conflict recorded:** the official subject brief states Paper 2 = 1.5 hours at both tiers; both corroborating mirrors state 1 hour 45 minutes. Resolved in favour of the directly-fetched official figure (90 minutes) since it is OFFICIAL_HOST and there was no independent third source to arbitrate between it and the two mirrors, which may share a common secondary error -- the conflicting figure is recorded in the record's own `internalNotes`, not silently discarded.

**Modeled as a `future` (not `current`) record -- 1 subject:**
- **Psychology** -- confirmed a genuine syllabus transition in progress: the currently-active course (first assessment 2019) is being taught out; a new course (first assessment 2027) was launched February 2025. IB's own public curriculum-updates page for this subject reproduces the new course's complete assessment-outline tables, including every mark total, directly and in full -- no mirror needed at all, `sourceConfidence` and `mirrorSourceUrl` both correctly omitted. This new record is deliberately typed `specStatus: 'future'`, not `'current'`, since it is not yet the syllabus current students sit. The currently-active 2019 syllabus is NOT modeled: its own public subject brief gives weighting/duration but not marks, and a real May-2019 markscheme mirror found this session confirms only Paper 2's mark structure (22 marks/question) for that outgoing course, not Paper 1 or Paper 3 -- a genuine, tracked gap, not silently dropped.

**Deferred -- 1 subject:**
- **Computer Science** -- confirmed the same kind of syllabus transition as Psychology (mid-transition, first assessment 2027 for the incoming course), but unlike Psychology, no source (official or mirror) was found this session giving reliable Paper 2 or Internal Assessment marks for either the outgoing or incoming course, despite solid Paper 1 figures for the incoming course. Per this batch's own decision rule (a full or partial record requires every component of at least one full tier to reach `authentic-mirror-high-confidence` or better; `marks` has no "unknown" representation), this subject stays `NOT_YET_MODELED`. Not attempted further, no guessed marks introduced.

**Coverage after this batch:** 159 of 160 ACTIVE matrix combinations now have a real, sourced assessment record (up from 154/160 after D-128) -- 5 new full/future records this batch. 1 remains `NOT_YET_MODELED` (Computer Science), a genuine, tracked, honestly-reported gap.

**Verification gate, run in full:** `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/validate-assessments.mjs` (all 14 checks pass, including the new check [14]; coverage line reads "159 / 160 ACTIVE combinations have a real, sourced assessment record. 1 are NOT_YET_MODELED"); `npm run validate:academic` (full chain, clean); `npm run build` (1728 pages, clean); `npm run audit:all` (all sub-audits clean, including `audit:content-integrity`'s internal-note-leakage scan across all 1728 built pages -- 0 problems, no script/file-path/decision-ID leakage into public `notes` text); `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs` (35/35, up from 32/32 -- the 3 new D-129 categories plus every pre-existing category, no regressions, source files verified byte-identical after every mutation/restore cycle); `npm audit` (0 vulnerabilities); `npx astro check` (0 errors, 0 warnings, pre-existing unrelated hints only).

**Not yet done / explicitly out of scope this round:** Computer Science remains `NOT_YET_MODELED` for the reason stated above. Psychology's currently-active (2019) syllabus remains unmodeled -- the `future` record above covers only the incoming 2027 course; a future session could close that specific gap by sourcing Paper 1/Paper 3 marks for the outgoing course from the same M19/3/PSYCH markscheme family this session partially traced. `docs/reports/academic-coverage-report-v1.2.json` was regenerated as part of `npm run build`'s own pipeline; no hand-editing performed.

**Owner authority:** carries forward the owner's evidence-policy-widening decision described above, made directly this session; no further owner input was sought mid-batch.

## D-130 — Full audit and remediation of the bulk-content automation's entire body of work (155 commits, 982 files), superseding the 4 Sept baseline's stale "49 undocumented commits, out of scope" assumption

**Date:** 2026-09-05
**Trigger:** Direct owner instruction, relayed via the orchestrating session: the 4 Sept baseline audit had flagged "49 undocumented bulk-content commits" from an automated content-generation process and marked them out of scope, on the assumption they belonged to a different Claude instance. The owner confirmed that assumption was wrong and asked for a full audit and remediation of the entire body of work. The orchestrating session had already re-derived the true scope (the automation was still running when the 49 figure was measured, so it was stale immediately) and handed this session a verified reconstruction to audit against, rather than re-deriving it from scratch.

**Scope reconstruction, independently re-verified before use.** The handed-off reconstruction — commits matching `^Deepen`, `^content(academic): deepen`, `^Weekly study guides`, `^Add [0-9]+.*deepening`, `^content: deepen`, `^Expand`, `^Fill .*depth gap`, `^Fill missed`, `^Regenerate coverage report after merge`, `^Build missing`, `^Top up` (case-insensitive, subject-anchored) from `b0b47035af631d886a9968e13d1ea7c5ca15c2fe~1` to `HEAD` — was recomputed independently with the exact same `git log --extended-regexp --grep` command and diffed byte-for-byte against the handed-off list: **0 lines of difference**. The 982-file union (via `git show --no-commit-id --name-only` per commit, unioned and filtered to files still present on HEAD) was likewise recomputed and diffed: **0 lines of difference**. **Confirmed exact: 155 commits, 982 files** (974 under `src/content/resources/`, 8 infrastructure files: `docs/decision-log.md`, `docs/reports/academic-coverage-report-v1.2.{csv,json}`, `public/_redirects`, `public/llms.txt`, `scripts/check-duplicate-resource-scope.mjs`, `scripts/test-cross-board-regression.mjs`, `src/data/academic/syllabus-topics.ts`). The 15 excluded legitimate commits in the same date range (GSC dashboard, IB MYP/DP modeling, a vulnerability fix, a title-formatting fix, an already-reviewed duplicate-scope fix, and the separately-labeled "Weekly depth batch" resources) were left untouched, as instructed.

**Tier 1 — automated, exhaustive, all 974 content files:**
- **Near-duplicate detection:** wrote a shingled 8-word-gram Jaccard-similarity script (`/tmp/audit/near_dup.py`, not committed — a throwaway analysis tool, not a repo artifact), comparing every file against every other file of the *same* `resourceType`, with an inverted-index candidate-generation step to make the ~510k possible same-type pairs tractable. At a permissive 0.15 Jaccard threshold, only **3 candidate pairs** surfaced across the entire corpus. All 3 manually reviewed in full: IGCSE World History 1848-1914 vs. the sibling O-Level version (0.597), IGCSE vs. O-Level Islamiyat Paper 2 notes (0.204), and Edexcel vs. OCR GCSE Mathematics "Number" notes (0.156). All three are **false positives** — genuinely independent prose for distinct qualification codes (each citing its own correct spec code, series and, where applicable, an explicit "identical core content to sibling X" disclosure that Cambridge's own syllabi corroborate), not copy-paste padding. Zero genuine near-duplicates found.
- **Red-flag grep sweep:** all 974 files scanned for `TODO|FIXME|Lorem ipsum|\[insert|XXX` (0 hits) and for process-leakage language adjacent to what `audit-content-integrity.mjs`'s `INTERNAL_NOTE_PATTERNS` already blocks (`sub-batch`, `batch N/`, `depth gap`, `thin ACTIVE combinations`, `top-up`, `NOT_YET_MODELED`, `regenerate coverage`, etc. — 0 hits). A verbatim-repeated-line scan (lines >60 chars appearing in >=5 distinct files) found 23 repeated lines; all are legitimate, intentional boilerplate (the required per-practice-file copyright disclaimer, a citation-format convention, and revision-notes cross-link phrasing), not disguised padding.
- **Word-count distribution and claim-checking:** computed whole-corpus word counts (whitespace-split method, frontmatter excluded); n=974, min 875, max 1458, median 948.5 — a tight, deliberate band consistent with the automation's own "past 900 words" target, one file 25 words under 900 (never itself the subject of a 900-word claim, so not a bug). Cross-referenced all **56 commits** whose subject line explicitly claims a numeric word-count outcome ("... past/to 900 words", 555 (commit, file) pairs) against the file's *current* word count on HEAD: **0 of 555 are actually under 900 words** — every claim holds. (An initial pass using a stricter alphanumeric-token regex wrongly flagged 253 as under 900; cross-checked against plain `wc -w`, which showed the regex was simply a non-standard undercount — the standard whitespace-split method, matching `wc -w`, is what the report above uses.) Also spot-checked 98 commits with a leading numeric claim adjacent to resource/combination/file wording against actual files-touched counts; all 14 apparent mismatches were manually confirmed to be false positives of the check's own naive regex (picking up syllabus codes, batch numbers, or legitimate one-combination-many-files cases), not real bugs.

**Tier 2 — targeted deep read, 39 of 982 files (≈4%), explicit sample, not exhaustive.** Stratified by board (Cambridge 16, IB 12, OxfordAQA 10, AQA 10, Edexcel 10, OCR 8 planned; 39 actually read in depth before diminishing returns and budget were judged to outweigh reading the rest) weighted ~65% toward quantitative subjects (chemistry, physics, mathematics, biology, economics, accounting, business finance) per the brief, covering practice-questions, revision-notes, study-guides and subject-guides. For every quantitative file, every worked-example and answer-key calculation was independently redone by hand (stoichiometry, kinetics/equilibrium Kp/Kc, mechanics, nuclear decay/half-life, GCSE number/percentages/surds/bounds, IB DP momentum/collisions, break-even/ratios/current-and-acid-test-ratios, economics multiplier/elasticity, statistics weighted means). **Result: zero arithmetic or factual errors found** across all 39 files. Academic identity (subject/board/qualification/stage/topic matching frontmatter and the file's own body) was correct in all 39. Cited official sources (spec codes, series years, syllabus document titles) were checked against known real board specifications and found accurate in all 39; several history/Islamiyat/Pakistan Studies dates and figures were cross-checked against established historical record and found accurate.

**One genuine issue found and fixed: a stale, misapplied IB commercial-licensing disclaimer.** While reading `ib-dp-physics-forces-momentum-revision-notes.md`, noticed its "Official syllabus" footer stating "Marlbridge holds, or is in the process of obtaining, a formal license from the IB for commercial use of this guide." This hedge language originates in D-008 (22 Aug), when the licensing status was genuinely unresolved for the two IB DP subjects (Economics, Physics) built from the IB's *licensed, full internal* subject guides. **D-091 (1 Sept) confirms the owner resolved this** ("the licensing situation is now resolved... the automation exclusion is lifted"), making the hedge stale from that date forward. Searched all 106 IB content files: only **7** still carried the sentence, and only these 7 — every other IB file (built from the freely public, unrestricted subject-brief documents, which is the sourcing basis for all but the original two D-008 subjects) correctly carries no such disclaimer at all. Of the 7, **2 fall outside this audit's 982-file scope** (`ib-dp-economics-syllabus-guide.md`, `ib-dp-physics-forces-and-momentum.md` — pre-existing D-008 originals, never touched by the bulk-content automation) and were left alone per the audit's scope boundary. The remaining **5 are in scope** and were fixed by removing the stale sentence: `ib-dp-biology-theme-a-unity-diversity-practice.md` (the sentence didn't even apply here — this file is sourced from the public Biology subject brief, the same unrestricted category as every other undisclaimed IB file, so its presence was a copy-paste error, not a real disclosure), `ib-dp-economics-demand-supply-equilibrium-revision-notes.md`, `ib-dp-physics-forces-momentum-revision-notes.md`, `ib-dp-physics-kinematics-revision-notes.md`, `ib-dp-physics-syllabus-guide.md`. Two of the five were themselves the subject of `Weekly study guides` bulk commits *after* D-091's 1 Sept resolution date (`ib-dp-physics-forces-momentum-revision-notes.md`, published 2026-09-02) — the automation was still copying the stale hedge forward from the older sibling files it was "deepening," even after the underlying uncertainty it described no longer existed. **Trade-off disclosed rather than papered over:** removing this sentence drops `ib-dp-physics-syllabus-guide.md` from 913 to 892 words, below the 900-word bar its own originating "Expand batch 10... to 900+ words" commit had certified. Per this audit's explicit fix policy ("do NOT expand anything further"), no compensating filler was added — the file is a complete, substantively correct 892-word guide, and the regression is disclosed here rather than concealed by re-padding.
- **Not a recurring class, no new validator added.** This was one historical sentence, introduced once (D-008) and copied forward by the deepening automation into a small, now-fully-identified set of sibling files, not a generalizable bug pattern the corpus is at ongoing risk of reproducing — `audit-content-integrity.mjs`'s existing `INTERNAL_NOTE_PATTERNS` already target a different failure class (internal engineering artifacts), and this sentence, while stale, was a legitimate (if outdated) business/legal statement, not an engineering leak. Judged not to meet this audit's own bar for adding a durable validator.

**Explicitly NOT checked — do not represent this as exhaustive coverage:** the ~935 content files outside the 39-file Tier 2 sample received only the Tier 1 automated checks (near-duplicate signature, red-flag sweep, word-count-claim cross-reference) — genuinely useful, whole-corpus, but structurally incapable of catching a subtle factual or arithmetic error that doesn't manifest as duplication, a red-flag string, or a word-count mismatch. The owner's brief's own structural/systemic categories (rendered-label integrity, review-trust signal, accessibility, metadata/canonical duplication, sitemap/indexability, structured-data agreement, cross-board leakage, exact-syllabus-scope duplication) remain independently confirmed clean across all 982 files by the pre-existing site-wide tooling (`npm run audit:all`, `check-duplicate-resource-scope.mjs`), which this session re-ran rather than re-derived.

**Verification gate, run in full after the fix:** `npm run build` (1728 pages, clean); `npm run audit:all` (11/11 clean, including a fresh `audit:content-integrity` internal-note-leakage scan across all 1728 built pages); `npm run validate:academic` (all 13 assessment sub-checks + grade-thresholds + practice-bank + practice-question-schema, clean); `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs` (32/32 passed — the reporting tool's own summary line, not a fixed "35" figure); `npm audit` (0 vulnerabilities); `npx astro check` (0 errors, 17 pre-existing unrelated hints); `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-duplicate-resource-scope.mjs` (PASS, same allow-listed pairs as baseline, no new duplicates introduced). Fresh-clone check (`git clone` to a scratch directory + `npm ci` + full gate) run against the final committed state.

**Not yet done / explicitly out of scope this round:** the ~935-file gap in Tier 2 coverage stated above. The 2 out-of-scope stale-hedge files (`ib-dp-economics-syllabus-guide.md`, `ib-dp-physics-forces-and-momentum.md`) were deliberately left untouched — they predate the bulk-content automation this audit covers; fixing them is a legitimate follow-up but belongs to a differently-scoped session if the owner wants it. The 6 `NOT_YET_MODELED` IB DP assessment gaps (D-128) are unrelated to this audit and untouched.

**Owner authority:** explicit, direct instruction relayed via the orchestrating session, 2026-09-05, superseding the 4 Sept baseline's "out of scope" assumption about this same body of work.

## D-131 — `assessments.ts` corrupted on `main` by a silently-truncated API push; recovered in full, and large-file pushes moved off the GitHub Contents API

**Date:** 2026-09-05
**Trigger:** The owner asked this session to push the six-commit D-129/D-130 series directly, rather than continue the bundle-and-apply handoff used for D-127 through D-130. The session had a GitHub connector authenticated as the repository owner, so it pushed via the GitHub Contents API. That mechanism turned out to be structurally unsafe for this repository's largest data file, and `main` was left in a non-compiling state for part of the session.

**What went wrong, precisely.** The Contents API (`create_or_update_file` / `push_files`) has no append or patch mode: it replaces a file wholesale, so the *entire* new file content must be supplied as a single parameter — which, for a model-driven client, means the whole file has to be generated as output tokens in one message. `src/data/academic/assessments.ts` is 3,526 lines / 349,870 bytes, roughly 87,000 output tokens, well beyond a single response's output budget. The generation stopped mid-file and the call was nevertheless submitted and accepted. The failure mode is the dangerous one: **not an error, but a plausible-looking partial file**.

Sequence on `main`:
- `ee1b341` — validator check [14]. Pushed cleanly; content verified identical to the intended `dd8cfd7`. No issue.
- `c6bf48b` — intended to be the D-129 data commit. Wrote `assessments.ts` truncated at **750 of 3,526 lines**, ending mid-record inside an unclosed Cambridge O Level Geography object. Invalid TypeScript; `npm run build` and therefore the Cloudflare deploy from `main` would fail from this commit onward.
- `ebf8775` — a first hotfix attempt that, through an operator error in constructing the API call, contained the literal string `PLACEHOLDER` instead of file content. Strictly worse than what it replaced, and corrected within the same minute.
- `81b812a` — a deliberate, disclosed **stopgap**: the complete type/interface header and both helper functions restored verbatim from the last known-good blob (`fdfa9f3`), with `ASSESSMENTS` left as an **empty array**. Chosen to make `main` compile again immediately while the real data was recovered by a safe route. Its commit message stated the emptiness explicitly. Verified with `npx astro check` (0 errors) before being relied on. **No assessment record was invented to fill the gap at any point** — the file was honestly empty rather than plausibly wrong, which is the same principle this data file has applied to unsourced records since D-050.
- `2fb905c` — full recovery (below).

**How recovery was done, and why that route.** The content could not be re-transmitted through the same API for the same reason it failed the first time, and no lower-level git data API (blob/tree/commit creation) was exposed by the connector. Rather than shipping a restructured file — splitting the array across part-files purely to fit a transmission limit would have let a tooling constraint dictate the repository's data layout, and would have changed the shape the validator and every consumer see — recovery used real git: the reviewed handoff bundle already produced for this series (`marlbridge-combined-dp-and-bulk-audit.bundle`, HEAD `00393f0a6fd18592ef49513132dc0d41e54de725`) was verified with `git bundle verify`, fetched into a scratch clone on the owner's own machine, and `main`'s tree was set to the bundle tip's tree with `git read-tree --reset -u` and pushed with ordinary `git push` over the owner's existing credentials. **Zero file content passed through the model's output**, so the truncation failure mode was structurally impossible for this step rather than merely unlikely.

**Verification of the recovered state.** `git diff --stat 00393f0 origin/main` is empty — the pushed tree is byte-identical to the reviewed six-commit tip, on an independent machine from the one that pushed it. `assessments.ts` is back to 3,526 lines / 349,870 bytes. The nine changed files are exactly the expected set (`assessments.ts`, `syllabuses.ts`, `test-negative-validation-suite.mjs`, `decision-log.md`, and the 5 D-130 resource files); `scripts/validate-assessments.mjs` correctly shows no diff, having already landed intact via `ee1b341`. Full gate re-run on a **fresh `git clone` of the pushed commit** plus `npm ci`: `npm run build` (clean, `[build] Complete!`), `npm run validate:academic` (PASS, all 14 checks, coverage 159/160), `npm run audit:all` (exit 0, all sub-audits `PASS: 0 problem(s)`), `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs` (35/35), `npm audit` (0 vulnerabilities), `npx astro check` (0 errors, 0 warnings, pre-existing hints only). The live site was independently re-fetched afterwards and is serving the restored records (`/boards/ib/ib-dp/business/` renders the full SL+HL component table with its mirror-sourcing disclosure).

**Standing rule adopted for future sessions.** The GitHub Contents API is acceptable only for **small** files (roughly under 25 KB) and only with an immediate post-push `git fetch` + `git diff` against the intended content before the push is treated as done. Anything larger — and `assessments.ts`, `syllabuses.ts` and `docs/decision-log.md` are all far larger — must go through real git (`git push` from an authenticated clone, seeded by bundle or patch if the content originates in a sandbox). A push is not "successful" because the API returned a commit SHA; it is successful when the remote content has been diffed against the intended content and matched.

**Honest assessment of impact.** `main` did not compile from `c6bf48b` until `81b812a`. This is a static site whose last successful deployment continues to be served while a build fails, and the live site was confirmed healthy after recovery, so there is no evidence visitors saw a degraded site — but that is a property of the hosting model absorbing the mistake, not of the process being safe. Between `81b812a` and `2fb905c`, a deploy from `main` would have built successfully but published assessment tables for **zero** combinations rather than 159; that window was minutes, and the live check above confirms the current deployment carries the full data. Two of the three bad commits were avoidable by verifying before trusting the tool's success response, which is now the standing rule above.

**Not done / out of scope:** the pre-existing gaps recorded in D-129 and D-130 are untouched by this recovery — Computer Science (IB DP) remains `NOT_YET_MODELED`, Psychology's outgoing 2019 syllabus remains unmodeled, and the 2 out-of-scope stale-hedge files remain as D-130 left them. The three incident commits (`c6bf48b`, `ebf8775`, `81b812a`) were deliberately **not** rewritten out of history: `main` is a published branch, and an honest record of the failure is worth more than a tidy log.

**Owner authority:** the owner instructed this session to push directly, and then to fix the repository once the corruption was reported to them. Both the stopgap and the recovery route were chosen by the session and are disclosed here in full.
## D-133 — `syllabusFor` disambiguated by syllabus code; Cambridge O Level Urdu split into a dedicated 3248 record

**Date:** 2026-09-05
**Trigger:** External content audit (5 Sep 2026, E20) found that `o-level-cambridge-urdu-second-language-paper-2-grammar-writing-translation.md` and `o-level-urdu-second-language-paper-2-revision-notes.md` (both declaring `syllabusCodes: ["3248"]`, 2024-2026 series) rendered an "Official specification" link resolving to Cambridge O Level **First Language** Urdu's 2027 document (721463), not Second Language Urdu's own 2024-2026 document (634455).

**Root cause.** `syllabuses.ts` modeled Cambridge O Level Urdu as a single combined record (`code: '3247 / 3248'`, `subjectSlug: 'urdu-language'`) because both specifications share one subject slug on this site. `syllabusFor(board, qualification, subject)` matches only on that triple via `Array.find`, so every resource under `urdu-language` — regardless of its own declared `syllabusCodes` — resolved to the same single `officialUrl`, which happened to be the 3247 document. The combined record's own `notes` field correctly named the 3248 source as plain text, but that text was never wired to the rendered link.

**Fix.** Added a second `Syllabus` record (`code: '3248'`) with the correct 634455 URL, alongside the existing combined record (left unchanged, since it is still the correct resolution for the 3 genuinely-combined resources whose own `syllabusCodes` is `["3247 / 3248"]`, and for the 3247-only resource, which has no dedicated record and correctly falls back to it). `syllabusFor` gained an optional 4th parameter — the resource's own `syllabusCodes` — and now prefers an exact match on `Syllabus.code` when a board/qualification/subject combination carries more than one record, falling back to the first record when the parameter is omitted or nothing matches exactly. This is purely additive: every other call site (`subjects/[slug].astro`, the board/qualification/subject hub page, `practice/index.astro`, `practice/[code]/index.astro`, `validate-rendered-academic-labels.mjs`) does not pass the new parameter and is byte-for-byte unaffected. Only `src/pages/resources/[slug].astro` was updated to pass `d.syllabusCodes`.

**Verification.** Confirmed via `syllabusFor('cambridge', 'o-level', 'urdu-language', ['3248'])` resolving to the new record and `syllabusFor('cambridge', 'o-level', 'urdu-language', ['3247'])` / `(..., undefined)` / `(..., ['3247 / 3248'])` all resolving to the unchanged combined record, matching pre-fix behaviour exactly for every case except the one being fixed. Full site build and validation gate re-run clean (see the accompanying commit).

**Not done / out of scope:** no sitewide audit was run for other board/qualification/subject combinations that might carry a similarly-combined record for two distinct codes — this fix addresses the one instance the audit found. If another exists, the same `syllabusFor` code-disambiguation mechanism now generalises to it without further engineering changes; it would need only a new dedicated `Syllabus` record.

**Owner authority:** user-selected option "Fix all 44 confirmed errors, by priority order" (2026-09-05), continuing autonomously per that standing instruction.
## D-134 — Owner rescinds the D-092 blanket "Reviewed by teachers" claim: no blanket or non-attributed review claim is made or required

**Date:** 2026-09-05
**Trigger:** An external content audit (5 Sep 2026, finding U03) flagged that `reviewedByTeachers` (default `true` since D-092, 2026-08-31) asserted, across all 1,251 published study resources, a blanket "Reviewed by teachers" trust claim that no per-resource evidence backs -- distinct from, and far broader than, the QIGT named-reviewer system, which as of this session still had 0 of 1,251 resources meeting its stricter bar. This session escalated the finding to the owner rather than resolve it unilaterally, since it turns on a real editorial/business fact (whether Marlbridge actually reviews every resource). Direct owner instruction, this session: "change the policy to no review required."

**Decision.** The D-092 blanket claim is rescinded. Marlbridge no longer states or requires a blanket, non-attributed "every resource has been reviewed by a teacher" claim. This does not touch the QIGT programme (`reviewStatus`/`reviewer`/`reviewedDate`, `scripts/validate-review-integrity.mjs`): that stricter, per-resource, named-and-accountable reviewer system, and the "Reviewed by [Name]" byline / schema.org `editor` claim it gates, are completely unaffected -- a real reviewer credit still displays wherever a real reviewer record exists, exactly as before.

**Implementation.**
- `src/content.config.ts` -- `reviewedByTeachers` default changed from `true` to `false`; doc comment rewritten to record the rescission. The field is kept (not deleted) so a specific, individually-documented exception remains possible without a schema change, but it is no longer read by any public-facing template.
- `src/pages/resources/[slug].astro` -- removed the "Reviewed by teachers" trust-line paragraph and its `{d.reviewedByTeachers && (...)}` gate. The syllabus-alignment sentence ("Aligned to ... Official specification ...") and the "Report a correction" link that were bundled in the same conditional block are unrelated to the review claim and are now rendered unconditionally, so removing the retired claim does not also remove that unrelated, genuinely useful provenance content.
- `scripts/audit-review-coverage.mjs` -- flipped from asserting the blanket claim IS present everywhere to guarding against it reappearing: no resource file may set `reviewedByTeachers: true` without a documented exception, no built resource page may render the retired "Reviewed by teachers" string, and the editorial policy page may not restate the rescinded claim.
- `src/pages/legal/editorial-policy.astro` -- "Academic review policy" section rewritten to drop the "All Marlbridge study resources are reviewed by teachers" sentence and describe the policy as it now actually is: no blanket claim, author-checked-against-syllabus as the baseline, and the named QIGT second-reviewer step (unchanged) as the only credited "reviewed by" claim the site makes. `lastUpdated` bumped to 5 September 2026.
- `scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs` `[AA]` -- fixture flipped to match: it now reinserts the retired trust line into a built page and confirms `audit-review-coverage.mjs` catches the regression, rather than removing it and confirming absence is caught.

**Verification gate, run in full:** `npx astro check`, `npm run validate:academic`, `npm run build`, `node scripts/test-cross-board-regression.mjs`, `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs`, `node --experimental-strip-types --test functions/api/__tests__/*.test.mjs`, `npm audit`, `npm run coverage:academic-v2`, `node scripts/check-duplicate-resource-scope.mjs` -- see the accompanying commit for exact results.

**Not done / out of scope:** the QIGT named-reviewer programme itself (which resources get a real, credited reviewer, and when) is untouched and outside this decision's scope -- this decision only retires the separate, blanket, non-attributed claim D-092 introduced.

**Owner authority:** explicit, direct instruction, 2026-09-05 ("U03 change the policy to no review required"), in response to this session's own escalation of audit finding U03.

## D-135 — Owner rescinds the D-008 "Marlbridge has or is pursuing a formal IB license" wording: no IB license is claimed or required

**Date:** 2026-09-05
**Trigger:** An external content audit (5 Sep 2026, finding U02) flagged that internal sourcing-provenance `notes` fields on the IB DP Economics and Physics records (`src/data/academic/{syllabuses,syllabus-topics,assessments,boards}.ts`) -- written under D-008 (2026-08-22) on the strength of the owner's chat confirmation that "Marlbridge has or is pursuing a formal IB license" for those two subjects' full guide PDFs -- render PUBLICLY (via `src/pages/boards/[board]/[qualification]/[subject].astro` and `src/pages/boards/index.astro`, which both display a syllabus/board's `notes` field directly on the live site) as ambiguous, unresolved-sounding licensing language on a business/legal fact a visitor has no way to verify. This session escalated the finding rather than resolve it unilaterally, since only the owner can settle whether Marlbridge actually holds, needs, or claims such a license. Direct owner instruction, this session: "change the internal license policy to no license required."

**Decision.** The "Marlbridge has, or is pursuing, a formal IB license" framing is retired. Going forward, Marlbridge does not claim to hold, or to be pursuing, any formal license from the IB, and no such license is treated as required for the site's IB content. This is consistent with, and completes, the direction already set by D-127 (2026-09-04): D-127 established that IB's own freely public specimen exam papers, paired with the freely public subject briefs, are a sufficient primary source for new DP assessment records without needing the licensed guide at all -- but D-127 explicitly declined to retroactively reword the original DP Economics/Physics `notes`, reasoning that doing so "would itself violate this repo's own accuracy discipline" by implying a different sourcing history than what actually happened. That reasoning governed *silently rewriting history*; it does not extend to today's decision, which is an explicit, dated, current-tense owner policy statement layered on top of the historical sourcing note, not a rewrite of it.

**Implementation.** Every `notes` field asserting "Owner confirmed a formal IB license... has or is pursuing..." (or minor variants) had a policy sentence appended or substituted, making clear that as of 2026-09-05 no such license is claimed or required, while leaving the historical sourcing fact (these two records were originally built from the full subject-guide PDFs) intact and undisputed, per D-127's own precedent of disclosing rather than concealing sourcing history:
- `src/data/academic/boards.ts` -- IB board record's `notes`.
- `src/data/academic/syllabuses.ts` -- DP Economics and DP Physics syllabus records' `notes` (2 fields).
- `src/data/academic/syllabus-topics.ts` -- DP Economics, DP Physics, DP Chemistry and DP Computer Science topic records' `notes` (4 fields; the latter two only cross-referenced the Economics entry's wording rather than repeating it, and are updated the same way).
- `src/data/academic/assessments.ts` -- DP Economics and DP Physics assessment records' `notes` (2 fields).

**Verification gate, run in full:** `npx astro check`, `npm run validate:academic`, `npm run build`, `node scripts/test-cross-board-regression.mjs`, `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs`, `node --experimental-strip-types --test functions/api/__tests__/*.test.mjs`, `npm audit`, `npm run coverage:academic-v2`, `node scripts/check-duplicate-resource-scope.mjs` -- see the accompanying commit for exact results.

**Not done / out of scope:** whether Marlbridge should, as a matter of copyright compliance, actually stop using the two guide PDFs as a sourcing basis for these two existing records is a separate, substantive licensing/compliance question this decision does not resolve -- it only retires the specific public-facing "license" wording the audit flagged as ambiguous. No IB content was removed, and no new sourcing was performed for these two records.

**Owner authority:** explicit, direct instruction, 2026-09-05 ("U02 change the internal license policy to no license required"), in response to this session's own escalation of audit finding U02.

## D-137 — U05: precise `syllabusTopics` mapping added where the official taxonomy actually supports it; the rest correctly left syllabus-wide

**Date:** 2026-09-05
**Trigger:** An external content audit (5 Sep 2026, finding U05) flagged 122 resources with a specific `topic:` display label in frontmatter but no structured `syllabusTopics` entry, meaning their topic claim is not cross-validated at build time against `src/data/academic/syllabus-topics.ts`. Owner instruction, this session: "U05 do what you see fit."

**Analysis.** Of the 122, 60 have a blank or explicitly whole-syllabus `topic` label (e.g. "Full syllabus (...)", "Full framework (...)") -- these are correctly left with no `syllabusTopics` entry; that is the valid, intended state for a genuinely syllabus-wide resource, not a gap. Of the remaining 62 naming a specific topic, only 14 sit under a board+subject+qualification combination that `syllabus-topics.ts` actually has a taxonomy entry for (AQA A-Level Sociology; AQA GCSE English Language; IB DP Chemistry; IB DP Computer Science; OCR GCSE Chemistry; OxfordAQA IGCSE Chemistry). The other 48 -- the entire IB DP cluster outside Chemistry/Computer Science (Biology, Business, ESS, Geography, Global Politics, both Language A courses, Language B, both Mathematics courses, Psychology, World History), the entire IB MYP cluster (Mathematics, Design, Individuals & Societies, Language Acquisition, Sciences), OCR A-Level Chemistry, and OxfordAQA A-Level Chemistry -- have literally no `syllabus-topics.ts` entry for that board+subject+qualification at all yet. `scripts/validate-academic-content.mjs` fails the build on any `syllabusTopics` entry for a combination with no taxonomy row ("no official topic taxonomy for board(s) ... + subject ... + qualification ..."), so precise mapping for those 48 is not an editorial choice available today -- it requires first building out 16 new taxonomy entries in `syllabus-topics.ts`, a substantially larger undertaking outside this finding's scope. They are correctly left with no `syllabusTopics` entry, the same valid default as the 60 syllabus-wide resources.

**Fix.** Added a `syllabusTopics` frontmatter entry, mapped to the real topic (and, where applicable, subtopic) slug in `syllabus-topics.ts`, to 14 resource files: `a-level-sociology-methods-in-context-{practice,revision-notes}.md` (topic `paper-1-education-theory-methods-7192`, subtopic `methods-in-context-7192`), `gcse-english-language-paper-1-{practice,revision-notes}.md` (topic `paper-1-explorations-in-creative-reading-and-writing-8700`), `ib-dp-chemistry-reactivity-3-mechanisms-revision-notes.md` (topic `ib-dp-chemistry-reactivity-3`), `ib-dp-computer-science-b2-programming-revision-notes.md` (topic `ib-dp-computer-science-theme-b`, subtopic `ib-dp-computer-science-b-2`), `ocr-gcse-chemistry-atomic-structure.md` and `gcse-chemistry-atomic-structure-{practice,revision-notes}.md` (topic `topic-c1-particles-j248`), and `oxfordaqa-igcse-chemistry-quantitative-{chemistry,practice,revision-notes}.md` (topic `quantitative-chemistry-9202`).

One initially-planned mapping was reverted: `gcse-history-historic-environment-{practice,revision-notes}.md`'s CSV topic label ("The Historic Environment Study") has no distinct slug in the AQA GCSE History taxonomy -- it is only mentioned in that record's free-text `notes`, not itemised as its own topic or subtopic -- so the only available slug was the same topic-level `understanding-the-modern-world-8145` already used, correctly, by the differently-scoped `gcse-history-understanding-modern-world-revision-notes.md`. Adding it made `scripts/check-duplicate-resource-scope.mjs` flag a false duplicate-scope collision between two genuinely different resources. Rather than force an imprecise mapping to satisfy this finding, both Historic Environment files were left with no `syllabusTopics` entry, consistent with the same "don't invent taxonomy precision that doesn't exist" principle applied to the 48 combinations above.

**Verification gate, run in full:** `npx astro check`, `npm run validate:academic`, `npm run build`, `node scripts/test-cross-board-regression.mjs`, `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs`, `node --experimental-strip-types --test functions/api/__tests__/*.test.mjs`, `npm audit`, `npm run coverage:academic-v2`, `node scripts/check-duplicate-resource-scope.mjs`, `npm run audit:all` -- see the accompanying commit for exact results.

**Not done / out of scope:** building the 16 missing `syllabus-topics.ts` taxonomy entries (IB DP: 10 subjects; IB MYP: 5 subjects; OCR A-Level Chemistry; OxfordAQA A-Level Chemistry) so the remaining 48 resources can eventually get a precise mapping too. That is genuinely new sourcing work -- researching and transcribing each board's real, current topic/subtopic breakdown -- not a frontmatter edit, and is out of scope for this finding.

**Owner authority:** direct instruction, 2026-09-05 ("U05 do what you see fit").

## D-140 — Auditor coordination round: four repo-wide "bulk sweep" defect patterns fixed (E218/E229/E231/E242/E253/E262, I108/I111/I117/I118/I124, Q107 investigated-and-closed) across 26 files, following the second audit instance's own cross-family re-screen

**Date:** 2026-09-06
**Trigger:** The owner relayed a message from the second external audit instance itself, sent in response to a direct question about coordination protocol. The auditor: (1) disclosed its working copy (`repository-current-files`) is a frozen checkout from 5 September that cannot self-refresh, so its "still open" verdicts and quoted line numbers drift from the live repo as fixes land -- confirming, from the auditor's own side, the staleness this session had already caught independently for E01 under D-139; (2) requested a lighter coordination protocol going forward -- finding ID, commit SHA, and one line on what changed, rather than being sent file edits, since it verifies independently and does not want its own `outputs/`/`work/` touched; (3) restated its "fix the defect everywhere it recurs, not just the named file" finding from its own family re-screen (10 of 78 sibling resources across 7 of 42 "verified-fixed" findings still carried the corrected defect -- the same lesson already absorbed as E208 under D-139); and (4) named four specific, already-diagnosed repo-wide defect patterns with finding IDs attached, inviting a direct sweep rather than a full re-read of the audit's newest range.

**Audit-reliability re-check.** As with every prior batch, the audit's own quoted line numbers were treated as approximate rather than authoritative, given the auditor's admitted frozen snapshot. This was borne out directly: E242's second citation (`ocr-gcse-biology-scaling-up.md#L125`) no longer matched at that line on live `main` (the real text was at line 142) because an unrelated intervening edit had shifted it -- the defect itself was still present and was fixed at its actual location. No finding in this batch was skipped or mis-fixed because of stale line numbers; each was re-grepped against live `main` before editing.

**Course-correction caught during this session's own reasoning, before any wrong edit was made.** This session's first pass at bulk-sweep pattern 1 (practical-work terminology) assumed, from general knowledge of English reformed-2016 GCSE science specifications, that OCR GCSE Biology/Physics (J247/J249) genuinely uses "required practicals" and should be left untouched, unlike OCR's A-level qualifications. Reading the audit's own primary-source-cited findings (E218, E242) directly contradicted this: OCR Gateway GCSE also organises practical work into Practical Activity Groups (a minimum of eight), not a "required practicals" list, and the named experiments the resources quote sit in the specification's "Practical suggestions" column, explicitly described there as a supplementable starting point rather than an examined checklist. The assumption was discarded in favour of the audit's cited specification-page evidence before any file was touched, and all four affected OCR GCSE files (not just the OCR A-level pair originally identified) were corrected.

**Findings addressed, by pattern:**
- **Practical-work terminology (E218, E242, I111, I118)** -- "required practical(s)" / "core practical(s)" reworded to the board-correct model in 9 files: two OCR GCSE Physics files (`ocr-gcse-physics-forces.md`, `ocr-gcse-physics-forces-revision-notes.md`) and two OCR GCSE Biology files (`ocr-gcse-biology-scaling-up.md`, `ocr-gcse-biology-scaling-up-revision-notes.md`) reworded to Practical Activity Groups (PAGs); two OCR A-level files (`ocr-a-level-biology-development-of-practical-skills.md`, `ocr-a-level-physics-development-of-practical-skills.md`) had a stray "core practical" reworded to PAG language (both files otherwise already used the correct Practical Endorsement framing); three Cambridge files (`a-level-biology-enzymes.md`, `igcse-biology-movement-cells-revision-notes.md`, `igcse-biology-movement-into-and-out-of-cells.md`) reworded away from the "required practicals" branded list Cambridge does not use, to "practical investigations" language consistent with Cambridge's own Paper 5 (Practical Assessment / Practical Test) and Paper 6 (Alternative to Practical) framework. Verified via WebSearch against OCR's own PAG/Practical Endorsement documentation and Cambridge's own 9700/0610 syllabus and learner-guide pages before editing (see chat citations). OCR GCSE's use of PAGs (not "required practicals") was confirmed directly from the audit's own specification-page citations, correcting this session's own initial, WebSearch-summary-based assumption to the contrary.
- **Domestic UK exam codes in International resources (E229, E262)** -- 2 files (`edexcel-a-level-biology-molecules-transport-revision-notes.md`, `edexcel-a-level-chemistry-bonding-revision-notes.md`) had frontmatter `description` fields citing domestic Pearson UK GCE codes (9BN0, 9CH0) corrected to the correct Pearson Edexcel International A-Level codes (YBI11, YCH11) already declared in each file's own `syllabusCodes` field. A repo-wide grep for the same defect against every other domestic Pearson code (9BI0, 9PH0, 9EC0, 9MA0, 9FM0, 9GE0, 9HI0) found no further instances.
- **Superseded specification versions cited as current (E231, E253, I117)** -- three separate OCR/Cambridge families corrected: six OCR GCSE Chemistry (Gateway J248) files updated from "Version 3.6" to "Version 4.0 (August 2026)" in frontmatter `syllabusSeries` and closing source notes (E231); three OCR A-Level Biology (H420) "Foundations in Biology" family files corrected from a fabricated qualification history (a false claim that a "2017-2024" specification was superseded and retired, when H420 has had one continuous specification since first teaching September 2015, periodically amended) and an outdated "Version 3" to the current "Version 4.1, April 2026" citation (E253); one Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610) file's source note corrected from "Version 2, published December 2025" to "Version 3, published August 2026" (I117).
- **"Section A" mislabelled as short-answer when it is multiple-choice in the real papers (I108, I124)** -- three practice-question files (`ocr-gcse-biology-cell-level-practice.md`, `ocr-a-level-biology-practical-skills-practice.md`, `ocr-a-level-biology-foundations-practice.md`) each carried "## Section A" / "## Section B" headings above written short-answer questions, falsely implying the paper structure of the real OCR exams (where Section A is multiple-choice, worth 15 marks). Fixed via the auditor's own stated alternative remedy -- dropping the section headings entirely, since questions were already independently numbered and no other page content referenced "Section A/B" -- rather than fabricating new multiple-choice items to fill a 15-mark section, which would have required inventing assessable content beyond this session's ability to verify against a real past paper.
- **Q107 investigated and closed with no code change.** Q107 flagged, as an explicitly unconfirmed claim (the auditor's own text: "recorded as a claim that could not be confirmed rather than as an established error"), that five OxfordAQA A-Level Biology (9610) files citing "Version 5.1" might be citing a version ahead of what the auditor's fetch of the specification PDF actually served (which showed Version 4.2). **Two regressions caught and fixed before this decision's commit, neither introduced by the batch-fixing work itself:**

Fixed by correcting the map entry to the proper forward direction (old slug to new slug, matching every other rename in the file) and regenerating `public/_redirects`.
3. **A duplicate page title from the same merge**, unrelated to any J-batch content: an upstream commit added a new Cambridge IGCSE Accounting practice-questions resource with an identical, unprefixed title to a pre-existing OxfordAQA sibling on the same topic. Caught by `audit:metadata` (part of `audit:all`). Fixed by prefixing the newly-added Cambridge resource's title with "Cambridge," matching the established board-disambiguation convention already used by its own revision-notes sibling.

**Two registry gaps and one truncation-collision caught by the validation gate, all fixed before commit:**
1. **Wrong subtopic slug.** E291's fix (adding O-Level Economics 2281's missing sub-topic 1.4 to `the-basic-economic-problem.md`) used the slug `production-possibility-curve-diagrams`, which is actually the *IGCSE* 0455 sibling's registered slug in `syllabus-topics.ts`; the O-Level 2281 registry entry uses `production-possibility-curve-ppc-diagrams`. Caught by `validate:academic`'s syllabus-topic-reference check; corrected to the right registry slug.
2. **Unregistered Pearson unit-entry codes.** E316/Q149's fixes correctly replaced the qualification-level "cash-in" codes (YBS11, YEC11) that six Edexcel International A-Level Business/Economics resources had been wrongly citing for single-unit content with the real per-unit entry codes (WBS11, WBS12 for Business; WEC11/01, WEC12/01 for Economics) -- both verified against the live Pearson specification PDFs. `syllabuses.ts` only stores one qualification-level `code` per entry, so the code-reference and (once that passed) cross-board-integrity validators both failed on the new unit codes. Fixed by extending both affected `syllabuses.ts` `code` fields (and the corresponding `syllabusCode` fields in `syllabus-topics.ts`, which the cross-board-integrity check requires to match exactly) to the site's existing "multiple genuine codes, `/`-separated" disclosure convention already used for dual-specification transitions (e.g. `9625 / 9725`) -- `'YBS11 / XBS11 / WBS11 / WBS12'` and `'YEC11 / XEC11 / WEC11/01 / WEC12/01'` respectively.
3. **A meta-description truncation collision from unrelated upstream content.** `npm run audit:all`'s metadata audit flagged 6 duplicate rendered `<meta name="description">` tags across 12 pages -- all from an IB MYP "criteria in practice" resource family added by concurrent upstream content-expansion commits (merged into this branch during this decision's own drift-check), not from this decision's own fixes. Each guide/revision-notes pair (and one cross-subject practice-file pair) shared an identical long opening clause that, once the site's 165-character meta-description truncation (`src/utils/seo/meta.ts`) cut the tag, left the two pages' rendered snippets byte-identical even though their full frontmatter descriptions differ. Fixed by rewording 5 revision-notes siblings to open with "Condensed, criterion-by-criterion revision notes on..." instead of repeating the guide's "Worked, criterion-by-criterion guidance on...", and 2 cross-subject practice-file siblings to name their MYP subject earlier in the sentence, so each pair diverges well inside the 165-character window. This is the same class of issue as D-141's duplicate-title regression (D-141 note 3) -- unrelated upstream content colliding with a pre-existing sibling, caught by the validation gate rather than the batch's own fixing work.

**Merge discipline:** origin/main had advanced by 20 unrelated commits (weekly content-depth and word-count-expansion work) by the time this decision's 260-ID fix pass was ready to commit. `git diff --name-only HEAD origin/main` vs `git status --short` found 6 overlapping files (5 content files plus the generated `public/_redirects`). Since git refuses to merge with uncommitted changes present on overlapping paths, this decision's fixes were committed first (`6d3286a`), then `origin/main` was merged (`10bf4a4`, clean auto-merge on all 6 overlapping files, no conflict markers) -- and, per the lesson recorded in D-141, every one of this decision's fix signatures in the 5 overlapping content files (`a-level-economics-government-intervention-revision-notes.md`, `a-level-mathematics-pure-mathematics-2-revision-notes.md`, `ib-dp-economics-syllabus-guide.md`, `mathematics-graphs-curves-revision-notes.md`, `o-level-business-people-in-business-practice.md`) was individually re-verified present in the merged tree before proceeding, rather than trusting the clean exit code alone. All five survived intact.

Among three practical notes (the ledger going stale between pushes; the ledger's interactive HTML being costly for the auditor's own tooling to read compared to the plain `.md`; and a caveat needed on the "findings fixed" headline number — all addressed below), the auditor flagged a substantive correction: their own E335 finding, and this session's D-140 fix for I108/I124 before it, had both concluded that OCR's "Section A"/"Section B" headings on affected practice-question resources implied a paper structure OCR does not use, and resolved this by deleting the headings. The auditor now states this was wrong on both occasions: Section A and Section B are real structural units of the actual specification, verbatim and independently confirmable, so removing the headings hid the mislabelling without fixing the substantive problem — these resources still gave students zero practice of the multiple-choice format that opens every real paper for these qualifications.

**Independent re-verification before touching any file.** Rather than act on the correction alone, this was checked directly against primary sources via live web search: OCR GCSE (9-1) Biology A / Chemistry A / Physics A (Gateway Science, J247/J248/J249) each split every paper into Section A (15 multiple-choice questions, 15 marks, four options A-D) and Section B (short-answer and extended six-mark questions, 75 marks); OCR A Level Biology A (H420) Papers 1 and 2, and OCR A Level Chemistry A (H432) Papers 1 and 2, use the identical Section A/B split. All four confirmed independently, matching both the auditor's claim and the primary-source citations already present in E335's own extracted text (which this session had read, but under-weighted relative to the "or delete the headings" alternative E335's own wording had offered alongside the "add real MCQs" option — the auditor's later message effectively retracts that alternative as insufficient).

**Scope judgment.** All 8 affected files (5 named directly by E335, 3 from D-140's I108/I124) are single-topic practice resources, not full mock papers — a real paper's 15-mark Section A draws on content across that paper's entire syllabus scope, not one topic. Reproducing an exact "15 marks" quota on a one-topic resource would itself misrepresent scope. The fix therefore adds a small, explicitly and honestly scoped multiple-choice sample (5 original one-mark questions, four options A-D, genuinely on-specification for that file's specific topic) rather than claiming to reproduce a full paper's Section A, with a sentence in each file saying so directly.

**Remediation (one commit, `3448871`, 8 files, dispatched as 3 parallel subagents by subject since the files share no overlap with each other):**
- `ocr-gcse-biology-scaling-up-practice.md`, `ocr-gcse-biology-cell-level-practice.md` (OCR GCSE Biology J247), `ocr-a-level-biology-practical-skills-practice.md`, `ocr-a-level-biology-foundations-practice.md` (OCR A Level Biology H420).
- `ocr-gcse-chemistry-purity-separating-practice.md`, `gcse-chemistry-atomic-structure-practice.md` (OCR GCSE Chemistry J248), `ocr-a-level-chemistry-amount-of-substance-practice.md` (OCR A Level Chemistry H432).
- `ocr-gcse-physics-forces-practice.md` (OCR GCSE Physics J249).

Each file gained a new "Section A — Multiple choice (topic sample)" section (5 original questions, matching the MCQ markdown format already established on this site by `a-economics-markets-in-action-practice.md`), with its existing question set retitled "Section B — Short answer and extended questions" and renumbered to follow; answers renumbered to match. Every file's question/answer numbering was verified programmatically to run 1..N with no gaps or duplicates before this decision's commit, since the site's practice-question schema validator requires this.

**Verification gate, run in full after merging one further unrelated upstream commit** (`c2338b1`, a word-count expansion pass, zero path overlap with these 8 files confirmed before merging): `npx astro check` (0 errors, 212 files), `npm run validate:academic` (all checks, PASSED), `npm run build` (pages built clean), `node scripts/test-cross-board-regression.mjs` (clean), `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs` (35/35), `node --experimental-strip-types --test functions/api/__tests__/*.test.mjs` (31/31), `npm audit --fetch-timeout=20000 --fetch-retries=2` (0 vulnerabilities), `npm run coverage:academic-v2` (regenerated), `node scripts/check-duplicate-resource-scope.mjs` (PASS, same allow-listed groups as before), `npm run audit:all` (all 11 sub-audits PASS, 0 problems).

**On the auditor's other two notes, addressed outside the repo:** (1) the published ledger will be regenerated after this push too, and going forward the plain `.md` ledger is being sent alongside the hosted page every time, since the auditor's own tooling reads the sandboxed HTML only as screenshots (text extraction and the accessibility tree both come back empty) while the flat file is what it actually verifies against; (2) the ledger's headline "findings fixed" count is being given an explicit caveat distinguishing "findings acted on in this project's own commits" from "independently verified closed by the auditor's own re-read" — the same distinction the auditor's own document already draws between its historical confirmed-error count and its currently-open count, so the two documents don't read as contradicting each other when placed side by side.
