## D-147 — `_redirects` breached Cloudflare's 2,000-static-rule ceiling (2,019 rules); narrowed the safe static block, rejected a wildcard rewrite of the flattened block, and handed off a Bulk Redirects CSV for the part that needs it

**Date:** 2026-09-07
**Trigger:** Following up on the owner's explicit "okay do it," given in response to this session's own D-146 operational flag ("`_redirects` at 1,969/2,000 (98.5%)... worth scheduling a migration to Bulk Redirects before it's hit"). Re-running `npm run audit:redirects` after merging 5 further upstream content-pipeline commits (new "exam-preparation" resources, `4a16117`..`f3efdaa`) found the ceiling had already been crossed: `_redirects` had 2,019 static rules, and the audit reported new redirects were being silently dropped, not merely approaching the limit.

**What was rejected, and why.** The obvious-looking fix is collapsing the dominant "Flattened resource URLs" block (1,583 of the 2,019 rules; `/resources/<type>/<slug>/ -> /resources/<slug>/` for a small fixed set of `<type>` values) into a handful of `:splat` or placeholder wildcard rules, one per resource type, since the destination never actually depends on the type segment. This was deliberately not done. `scripts/generate-redirects.mjs`'s own header comment is a direct, first-hand account that this exact two-segment `/resources/:type/:slug/` shape was already tried with Cloudflare's placeholder matching and failed in production — requests fell through to the single-segment rule and landed on the index page — which is why the file uses enumerated static rules at all. Reintroducing that pattern to buy headroom would risk reproducing a known, previously-shipped production bug, and this environment has no write-scoped Cloudflare API access (confirmed via `zone_details` — permissions are `#dns_records:read, #analytics:read, #zone:read, #member:read, #organization:read` only) to deploy and verify a different outcome before it ships to production traffic.

**What was done instead, in two parts:**

1. **Immediate, safe stopgap (shipped in this commit).** The "Consolidated resources" block was over-enumerating: for each of the 32 `CONSOLIDATED_RESOURCES` entries (old slug -> surviving resource, for genuinely deleted files), it emitted the bare old-slug rule plus a rule for all seven `RESOURCE_TYPES`, even though a resource can only ever have carried one `resourceType` before deletion. The actual former type of every one of the 32 old slugs was recovered from git history (`git show <delete-commit>^:src/content/resources/<slug>.md`, reading the `resourceType` frontmatter) — all 32 resolved cleanly, none required a fallback. `scripts/generate-redirects.mjs` now emits a new `CONSOLIDATED_RESOURCE_FORMER_TYPES` lookup and uses it to emit only the bare rule plus that one real former-type rule per old slug (falling back to all seven only if a future entry's former type can't be recovered from history). This cut the block from 256 to 64 lines — 192 rules removed — with zero behaviour change (the six dropped rules per entry were for type-prefixed URLs that no version of that resource was ever actually served or linked under). Re-running `npm run generate:redirects` and `npm run audit:redirects` confirmed the ceiling breach is resolved: 1,827 of 2,000 static rules (91%), back to a WARN rather than a hard breach, with the count independently corroborated by the raw rule-count grep against the generated file.

2. **Long-term fix, handed off (not executed by this session).** The 1,583-rule "Flattened resource URLs" block is the real, unbounded growth driver — every new resource the content pipeline adds costs one more rule here, and today's stopgap only buys time. Cloudflare's own documented answer for exceeding the `_redirects` ceiling is Bulk Redirects: an account-level product, evaluated in front of Pages, that uses the same enumerated (not wildcard) static source/target matching as the current file — so it does not carry the placeholder-matching risk documented above — and is not subject to the 2,000-rule ceiling (Free plan: 10,000 URL redirects across up to 5 lists, confirmed via Cloudflare's docs). This session's Cloudflare API access is read-only, so the Bulk Redirect List and Rule could not be created here. Instead: the current flattened-block content was exported as `marlbridge-bulk-redirects-flattened-resources.csv` (1,583 rows, Cloudflare's documented `<source_url>,<target_url>,<status_code>` CSV format, no header row, verified against the live regenerated `_redirects` file), delivered to the owner alongside a step-by-step dashboard setup guide (`marlbridge-bulk-redirects-setup.md`) covering prerequisites (DNS must be proxied through Cloudflare), the list-creation/import/rule steps, and verification. `scripts/generate-redirects.mjs`'s header comment was updated in place to record this account and to warn against removing the flattened-block emission loop until the owner has confirmed Bulk Redirects is actually live — removing it first would 404 all 1,583 of those legacy URLs immediately.

**Verification gate, run in full:** `node --check scripts/generate-redirects.mjs` (syntax), `npm run generate:redirects` (regenerated, byte count and rule totals sanity-checked), `npx astro check`, `npm run validate:academic` (all checks, PASSED), `npm run build`, `node scripts/test-cross-board-regression.mjs`, `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs` (35/35), `node --experimental-strip-types --test functions/api/__tests__/*.test.mjs` (31/31), `npm audit --fetch-timeout=20000 --fetch-retries=2` (0 vulnerabilities), `npm run coverage:academic-v2`, `node scripts/check-duplicate-resource-scope.mjs`, `npm run audit:all` (all 11 sub-audits, redirects sub-audit back to WARN not failure).

**Not done / explicitly deferred:** the flattened-block emission loop itself was left untouched in the generator — removing it is contingent on the owner confirming the Bulk Redirects List/Rule is live in the Cloudflare dashboard, which is outside this session's write access. No CSV rows were applied to Cloudflare; the CSV and guide are a handoff, not a completed migration.

**Owner authority:** direct continuation of the owner's "okay do it," given in response to this session's own D-146 flag.

## D-148 — Cloudflare Bulk Redirects migration completed and verified live; flattened-block emission loop removed from the `_redirects` generator (245 static rules, down from 1,969 two commits ago)

**Date:** 2026-09-07
**Trigger:** Direct continuation of D-147, which exported the 1,583-rule "Flattened resource URLs" block as a Cloudflare Bulk Redirects CSV and a dashboard setup guide, since this session's Cloudflare API access is read-only. The owner said "use the browser," authorizing browser automation (Claude in Chrome, against the owner's own already-authenticated Cloudflare dashboard session) to complete the parts of the migration that don't need write-scoped API access.

**What was done, via the browser, against the owner's own logged-in Cloudflare session:**
- Created a Bulk Redirect List (`marlbridge_flattened_resources`, described with a reference to this decision) under the account's Bulk Redirects section (account-level, not the zone's `_redirects` file).
- The CSV upload control itself couldn't be driven directly: the browser extension's file-upload tool was unavailable in this session, and desktop-level automation is deliberately restricted to read-only screenshots inside any browser window (by design, to prevent exactly this kind of blind credential/file exposure), so it couldn't drive the native file picker either. The owner completed the one manual step -- selecting `marlbridge-bulk-redirects-flattened-resources.csv` in the upload dialog -- and confirmed; the list's own item count (1,583) was then verified directly against the review screen before proceeding, matching the CSV exactly.
- Created a Bulk Redirect Rule (`marlbridge_flattened_resources_rule`) referencing that list, scoped to `marlbridge.com`. Before enabling it -- since this flips on live production routing for 1,583 URLs -- explicit confirmation was sought from the owner in chat rather than assumed from the earlier "use the browser" instruction; the owner confirmed "Yes, enable it now."
- Deployed the rule. The Bulk Redirects dashboard confirmed: 1 of 15 rules used, "Enabled"; 1 of 5 lists used, 1,583 of 10,000 items, list status "Active."
- Verified independently, not just trusted from the dashboard's own status label: navigated to three URLs picked at random from the CSV (`/resources/study-guides/igcse-english-literature-paper-4-unseen/`, `/resources/revision-notes/o-level-commerce-commercial-operations-revision-notes/`, `/resources/study-guides/energy-resources-and-efficiency/`) directly against live `marlbridge.com`. All three 301-redirected to their correct flat `/resources/<slug>/` target and rendered the correct page (titles matched the target resource in each case), confirming the migration was actually serving traffic correctly, not just configured.

**Follow-up code change, once the migration was confirmed live (not before -- doing this first would have 404'd all 1,583 legacy URLs the moment it shipped):** `scripts/generate-redirects.mjs`'s "Flattened resource URLs" emission loop was removed entirely, along with the now-dead code it existed to support: the `resources` slug list, the `resourceTypeOf()`/`resourceTypes` frontmatter-reading pair, and the now-fully-unused `TYPE_CHANGED_RESOURCES` map (the last real reclassification-redirect concern moves to the Bulk Redirect List itself going forward, edited directly in the Cloudflare dashboard rather than regenerated here). The `CONSOLIDATED_RESOURCES` / `CONSOLIDATED_RESOURCE_FORMER_TYPES` machinery from D-147 is untouched -- that block handles permanently-deleted/renamed resources redirecting to a *different* surviving slug, which is unrelated to the flattened-URL migration and still belongs in the static file. The unused `readFile` import was also dropped. The file's header comment was rewritten to record this account in place of the now-resolved ceiling-breach warning.

**Result:** `_redirects` dropped from 1,842 lines / 1,827 static rules (D-147's post-fix state) to 257 lines / 245 static rules (244 static + 1 wildcard, per `audit:redirects`'s own count) -- an 87% reduction, and Cloudflare's ceiling warning is gone entirely rather than merely deferred. The removed 1,583 rules are not orphaned: they live on, verified working, in the Bulk Redirect List.

**Verification gate, run in full:** `node --check scripts/generate-redirects.mjs`, `npm run generate:redirects` (245 static rules, sanity-checked against the raw file), `npm run audit:redirects` (PASS, 0 problems, no ceiling warning), `npx astro check` (0 errors, 212 files), `npm run validate:academic` (all checks, PASSED), `npm run build`, `node scripts/test-cross-board-regression.mjs`, `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs` (35/35), `node --experimental-strip-types --test functions/api/__tests__/*.test.mjs` (31/31), `npm audit --fetch-timeout=20000 --fetch-retries=2` (0 vulnerabilities), `npm run coverage:academic-v2`, `node scripts/check-duplicate-resource-scope.mjs`, `npm run audit:all` (all 11 sub-audits PASS, 0 problems -- `audit:internal-links` specifically confirmed 0 broken links after the removal, since the site never linked to the type-prefixed URLs internally in the first place; only external/legacy/bookmarked links ever used them, and those are now Bulk Redirects' responsibility).

**Not done / explicitly out of scope:** no change was made to the `CONSOLIDATED_RESOURCES` static-file mechanism (still appropriate for its narrower, different purpose). No further Cloudflare account configuration was touched beyond the one List and one Rule described above.

**Owner authority:** "use the browser" (authorizing the browser-automation approach to what D-147 had flagged as blocked on API access), followed by explicit, specifically-requested confirmation ("Yes, enable it now") before the one action in this round that changes live production routing.
## D-149 — Conversion & trust round: homepage repositioned on the tuition offer, one-to-one pricing surfaced, teacher profiles made decision-useful, trial journey given real published facts

**Date:** 2026-09-06

**Trigger:** An owner-commissioned review of marlbridge.com as a commercial site — "do more suitable students and parents choose Marlbridge, request a free trial, attend it, and enrol" — supplying a list of suspected defects to verify rather than to accept. Every item below was checked against the codebase at `f15e868` before anything was changed; the list is recorded here with what was found, including the items that turned out to be already handled.

**What was verified as still true (and fixed):**
- The homepage led with a mission statement ("Bridging Knowledge and Opportunity — everywhere a learner studies") and two browsing actions. The free trial — the site's actual primary conversion — appeared nowhere on the page. No teachers, no lesson format, no fees basis, no trial explanation.
- `/tutoring/` summarised fees as "charged per subject, per month" with the group-only multi-subject and sibling discounts. That is the GROUP basis only, on a page whose first listed mode is one-to-one tutoring — which is charged per class and carries no discounts. The one-to-one rates have existed in `src/data/pricing.ts` (`ONE_TO_ONE_PRICING`, D-012) since August and were never stated there.
- `src/content/programs/igcse.md` (and `o-levels`, `a-levels`) had two-sentence bodies with no lesson detail at all.
- `authors/[slug].astro` rendered a bio, a credentials line, then two long publication archives. The authors collection schema has held `subjectsTaught`, `yearsExperience`, `previousSchools`, `sourceUrl` and `verifiedOn` since v1.x WS4 — **the template rendered none of them.**
- `/trial/` published no response window, no trial duration, no trial format, and no statement of what happens after submitting.
- The resource-page tuition invitation was one generic line pointing at `/tutoring/`.
- `WhatsAppButton.astro` sent the same fixed message from every page on the site.
- `npm run audit:all` was **already failing on `main` before this round** — 6 duplicate meta descriptions across 12 IB MYP resource pages, which blocked the other 10 audits in the chain from running at all.

**What was verified as ALREADY handled, and deliberately left alone:**
- A gold "Free Trial Class" CTA already exists in the header and mobile menu (v1.x CLOSURE follow-up).
- Pricing already has a single validated source of truth with an FX-drift build gate (D-049).
- The review brief asked for structured qualification/board/subject/availability fields on the trial form. **This was explicitly declined**: D-047 removed exactly those fields on the owner's instruction that "student enquiry forms must contain only: Name, Email, Phone, Country, Message." The owner was asked directly about the conflict on 2026-09-06 and confirmed D-047 stands. The form is unchanged; everything around it was improved instead.

**Owner authority (all confirmed directly in chat, 2026-09-06):**
- Trial form keeps its 5 approved fields — D-047 stands, the review brief does not override it.
- Homepage: full reposition onto the tuition offer approved, with the vision / Learners Academy / schools material moved below the decision path rather than deleted.
- Response commitment: **email within two working days, WhatsApp within one working day.**
- Trial format: **matches the format being considered** — a group trial is a real group class, a one-to-one trial is an individual class. Duration is therefore derived from the already-published `classFormat`, not restated as a second number.

They were **not** duplicate source text: the descriptions differed only past the 165-character `metaDescription` truncation point, so the rendered snippets collided. The fix front-loaded the distinguishing detail (format for the revision-notes siblings, subject name for the practice pair) — same facts, reordered, no new claim. **On rebase this collided with D-144, which had diagnosed and fixed the identical defect concurrently.** `origin/main`'s wording was taken for all 7 files rather than re-litigating equivalent copy; `npm run audit:metadata` was re-run on the rebased tree to confirm the merged result still passes.

**Verification (all run on the final tree, not an intermediate one):** `npm run validate:academic` PASS; `npm run build` PASS (1,978 pages); `npm run audit:all` **PASS — an improvement on the pre-existing `main`, which failed this chain**; `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs` all categories pass; `npx astro check` 0 errors / 0 warnings; `npm audit --omit=dev` 0 vulnerabilities; functions unit tests 31/31. `audit:accessibility` PASS across 1,978 pages. Rendered HTML spot-checked on `/`, `/trial/`, `/programs/igcse/` and `/authors/muhammad-ghazali-siddiqui/`: exactly one `h1` each, no skipped heading levels, derived board list and teacher count correct, trial-context box `hidden` by default, and the a/an article helper correct across all six taught programmes (an earlier draft rendered "Try a IGCSE class first").

## D-150 — Learners Academy's results and reviews published under attribution (partial override of D-034); redundant header CTA removed; O Level past-paper wording made precise

**Date:** 2026-09-07

**Trigger:** Owner responses to the four open items left by D-149.

### 1. Results and testimonials — D-034's testimonial restriction lifted, with conditions

**Owner instruction (2026-09-07):** "Consented testimonials or case studies: you can use from learnersacademy.com.pk".

**What that overrides:** D-034 recorded that Learners Academy was approved as evidence for **pricing and faculty information only**, and that "its academic taxonomy, results, testimonials or unsupported claims are NOT imported." The owner has now lifted that restriction **for results and testimonials specifically**. The academic-taxonomy and unsupported-claims half of D-034 was not raised and **still stands** — Marlbridge's matrix remains its own.

**What was read, not assumed:** `https://learnersacademy.com.pk/results/`, fetched 2026-09-07. It is unusually disciplined source material: 51 grades from 44 students in the August 2026 season, published with the B's (16) and the single C left in, first name and initial only because some students are minors, and a stated check against the official Cambridge International Statement of Results where one was sent. The arithmetic was **re-derived rather than copied**: 4 + 30 + 16 + 1 = 51, and (4 + 30) / 51 = 66.7%, consistent with the published 67%.

**The attribution problem, and how it is handled.** These students studied at Learners Academy and these reviews were left about Learners Academy. Presenting them in Marlbridge's voice would misattribute another organisation's results — the same class of error the site already guards against when it insists a teacher's previous school is not an endorsement of Marlbridge. What makes publication honest is the relationship already stated on the homepage: Learners Academy is the founding academy behind Marlbridge and the same teachers now teach under the Marlbridge name. So the data lives in its own file (`src/data/learners-academy-evidence.ts`), **not** in `src/data/outcomes.ts`, and `AcademyResults.astro` names Learners Academy in the eyebrow, in the first sentence, and in a source line carrying the URL and the date it was read.

**`src/data/outcomes.ts` remains empty and stays in the homepage sequence.** Marlbridge's own consented outcomes are still a genuine gap; merging the two files would have hidden that gap rather than closed it.

**Explicitly NOT imported, and not to be added without a new decision:**
- **"4,200+ A & A* grades"** and **"9+ years teaching"** from the Learners Academy homepage — lifetime aggregates with no published basis, year or method. The results-season figures are checkable; these are not.
- **Any `AggregateRating` or `Review` JSON-LD.** The 4.6★/32 reviews figure is Learners Academy's Google rating for Learners Academy. Emitting it as structured data on a Marlbridge page would assert a review rating for the wrong entity — a fabricated rating in Google's terms however real the number is elsewhere. It is rendered as attributed plain text with a link out and **no schema whatsoever**; verified absent from the built HTML.
- **Full surnames**, for the same minor-safeguarding reason the source gives.

**Consent basis — raised explicitly, and answered.** The owner was asked directly, in a question that stated the concern rather than burying it: consent given to Learners Academy to publish on `learnersacademy.com.pk` is not automatically consent to republish under a different brand, and some of these students are minors. The owner was offered three options (publish in full / publish the grade spread but hold the four named quotes / hold all of it pending a permissions check) and chose **publish in full**, on the basis that he owns both organisations and is satisfied the original permission covers this use (2026-09-07).

**What that does and does not settle.** It is a real, informed authorisation from the person entitled to give it, and it is why this content ships. It is **not** a consent record this session inspected — no permission document was seen. If any family ever objects, the remedy is immediate removal of that entry from `src/data/learners-academy-evidence.ts`, which is why the data sits in one editable file rather than being written into page copy. The minor-safeguarding constraint (first name and initial only, never full surnames) travels with the data regardless of this authorisation and is not the owner's to waive on a student's behalf.

**Where it renders:** homepage (between "how it works" and the group/one-to-one comparison) and `/tutoring/`.

### 2. Header "Explore Programs" button removed

**Owner instruction:** "do as you see fit." Removed from `Header.astro` and `MobileMenu.astro`. It pointed at `/programs/`, already the first item in `primaryNav` inches away, so it was a second route to the same page competing visually with the trial CTA next to it. The header now carries exactly one action. **Nothing became unreachable** — Programs remains in the desktop nav and the mobile menu; verified in the built HTML (`Explore Programs` occurrences on the homepage: 2 → 0; `Free Trial Class`: 2, unchanged).

### 3. O Level "past-paper practice" wording

**Owner confirmation:** past-paper work is something done in class; a folder of past papers may be shared later for hosting. The claim was therefore accurate but ambiguous on a site that publishes zero past-paper resources and has deliberately removed that empty category from sitewide navigation. `o-levels.md`'s `shortDescription`/`description` now read "past-paper practice **worked through in class**", which cannot be read as a promise of downloadable papers.

**Past-paper hosting was NOT built.** No files exist yet, and `claude/section14-past-paper-audit-2026-09-01.md` records this programme's deliberately conservative position on past-paper material. Hosting third-party exam papers is a licensing question in its own right and needs its own decision when the folder actually arrives — it is not a side effect of a wording fix.

**Verification:** `npm run validate:academic` PASS; `npm run build` PASS; `npm run audit:all` PASS; `npm run check:duplicate-scope` PASS; `npx astro check` 0 errors / 0 warnings; negative-fixture suite all categories pass; functions unit tests 31/31; `npm audit --omit=dev` 0 vulnerabilities. Built HTML checked directly for the attribution sentence, the absence of rating structured data, and the removed header button.

## D-151 — Nouman Ahmed, Salman Ahmad and Hina Mogul pinned to the top of every public teacher listing

**Date:** 2026-09-08

**Trigger:** Owner instruction, with a screenshot of the "Who teaches …" block on a programme page: "always keep Nouman Ahmed, Salman Ahmad and Hina Mogul on top". Clarified in the same exchange that the list in the screenshot was the programme-page one (`ProgramTeachers.astro`, identifiable because its second line renders `subjectsTaught` rather than `role`), and that the rule applies to the teacher list on every programme.

**Scope decision — applied to all three listings, not just programme pages.** Teachers appear in three places, each with a different natural sort: the homepage band (`TeachersBand`, by recorded experience, truncated to six), the `/tutoring/` grid (alphabetical), and the programme-page block (by experience, filtered to that qualification's ACTIVE matrix subjects). "Always" was read as covering all three — a pin honoured on programme pages but not on the homepage or `/tutoring/` would be the same instruction visibly not applied two clicks away.

**Implementation:** `src/data/featured-teachers.ts` (new) holds `PINNED_TEACHER_SLUGS` and `sortPinnedFirst(entries, compare)`, which moves pinned authors to the front in the listed order and leaves the caller's own comparator to order everyone else. All three call sites now go through it. Deliberately one shared module rather than three hard-coded lists: a future contributor changing one component's sort cannot silently break the rule in the other two.

**What the pin does NOT do — the important constraint.** It only reorders teachers already eligible for a given list; it never inserts anyone. `ProgramTeachers` still filters to teachers whose own `subjectsTaught` matches an ACTIVE matrix subject for that qualification, so the pin cannot place Nouman Ahmed (Chemistry) on a programme whose active subjects do not include Chemistry, and cannot imply anyone teaches a subject they do not. A pinned teacher who is not eligible simply does not appear on that page, exactly as before. This was checked, not assumed — see verification.

**Note on the homepage band:** because it truncates to six, the pin changes *who is visible*, not merely the order. That is the intended effect of the instruction, but it is a real editorial consequence and is recorded here rather than left implicit.

**Failure behaviour, deliberately split:** at runtime a slug that no longer matches an author silently no-ops, so a broken pin can never take a page down. At build time `scripts/validate-pinned-teachers.mjs` (new; wired into `validate:academic`, also `npm run validate:pinned-teachers`) FAILS on a pinned slug that has no author file, is not `entityType: person`, is not `publicationState: published`, or is duplicated. Without it, a typo or a renamed/unpublished author would quietly drop an explicit owner instruction with nothing on the page to show it.

**Verification:** built HTML read directly for all three listings. Programme pages `/programs/igcse/`, `/programs/a-levels/` and `/programs/o-levels/` each now open `Nouman Ahmed | Salman Ahmad | Hina Mogul`, followed by the previous experience ordering (Iftikhar Azeemi, Azam Siddique, Muhammad Ghazali Siddiqui …); the homepage band opens with the same three; `/tutoring/` opens with the same three followed by the unchanged alphabetical remainder (Aizaz Raoof Ali, Ameer Hamza, Arslan Tanvir …). `npm run validate:pinned-teachers` PASS. Full gate on the final tree: `validate:academic` PASS, `build` PASS, `audit:all` PASS, `astro check` 0 errors / 0 warnings, negative-fixture suite all categories pass, functions unit tests 31/31.

## D-152 — Enquiry rate limiting was never actually running: `ENQUIRY_RATE_LIMIT` KV binding created, declared, and a validator added so a fail-open binding can never silently go missing again

**Date:** 2026-09-08

**Trigger:** While diffing the deployed Worker's bindings against `wrangler.jsonc` (during an unrelated deploy investigation), `wrangler versions view` showed the live Worker had exactly two bindings — `env.DB` and `env.ASSETS`. `functions/api/enquiry.ts` reads a third.

**What was actually wrong.** `functions/api/enquiry.ts` has called `checkRateLimit(env.ENQUIRY_RATE_LIMIT, ip)` since the endpoint was written, capping enquiry submissions at 5 per IP per hour. That binding was never declared in `wrangler.jsonc`, and `npx wrangler kv namespace list` returned `[]` — **no KV namespace existed on the Cloudflare account at all.** So `env.ENQUIRY_RATE_LIMIT` was always `undefined` in production and `checkRateLimit`'s first line, `if (!kv || !ip) return true`, returned `true` on every single request. The site has been running with **no enquiry rate limiting whatsoever**, while the source read as though it had some.

**Why nothing ever caught it.** The fail-open default is correct behaviour and was chosen deliberately — a KV outage should degrade rate limiting, never block a real family's enquiry. But fail-open is exactly what made this invisible: nothing threw, nothing logged, and no request behaved differently. A binding that *failed closed* would have been noticed on the first submission. No existing validator compared what the Worker reads against what the config provides, so the gap sat in the blind spot between the two.

**What shipped:**
- KV namespace `ENQUIRY_RATE_LIMIT` created (id `f1cee847b64448afb8bb30141dc6dc8e`) and declared in `wrangler.jsonc` with the reasoning inline. Fail-open is retained deliberately; Turnstile and the honeypot remain the primary spam defences and this is a second layer, not the first.
- `scripts/validate-worker-bindings.mjs` (new; wired into `validate:academic`, also `npm run validate:worker-bindings`): scans `functions/` and `src/worker/` for every `env.X` reference and fails the build unless each one is a binding declared in `wrangler.jsonc` or a name on an explicit `KNOWN_SECRETS` list. The three real secrets (`RESEND_API_KEY`, `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`, `GSC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`) are listed there because they are correctly set with `wrangler secret put` and must never be committed — confirmed present on the deployed Worker via `wrangler versions view`. Adding a name to that list is meant to be a conscious statement that it is a real externally-set secret, not a way to silence the check.
- README's environment-variable table and validation section updated to describe the binding and the new check.

**Verification, including the negative case:** with the new binding declared, `validate-worker-bindings.mjs` PASSES (3 declared bindings, 3 known secrets, 6 `env.` references). The `kv_namespaces` block was then temporarily deleted and the script re-run — it FAILED with `env.ENQUIRY_RATE_LIMIT is read in functions/api/enquiry.ts but is neither declared in wrangler.jsonc nor a known secret`, proving it catches the exact fault it exists to catch rather than merely passing; `wrangler.jsonc` was then restored and confirmed byte-for-byte identical (`cmp`). `npm run validate:academic` PASS on the final tree.

**Not yet live at time of writing.** The KV namespace exists on the account and the binding is committed, but the binding only takes effect on the next deploy. Until then production continues to fail open exactly as before — no regression, but no rate limiting either. See the deploy note below.

**Deploy context (separate issue, same session) — corrected below, same day.** This entry originally claimed the Git integration had "stopped firing" for `5e10f52`. That was wrong. Per this repo's append-only decision-log discipline, the error is corrected here rather than silently edited.

**Correction (2026-09-08, later the same day):** `wrangler deployments list` only lists successful deployments, so a build that fires and fails is invisible there — that gap produced the original misdiagnosis. Cloudflare's own dashboard Build History (`.../production/builds`), checked directly via the account owner's authenticated session, shows the Git integration never stopped firing:

- `5e10f52` (build `bd4d9be9`) DID trigger, visible in Build History 9 hours after merge. Initializing/Cloning/Installing/Building all succeeded, including a full `validate:academic` pass. Only the final Deploying step failed, 13 seconds in, with a transient Cloudflare-side error: `GET /accounts/.../workers/services/mb -> 503 Service Unavailable` ("upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers"). That is Cloudflare's own Workers API failing during wrangler's worker-name validation — not a config, credential, or code fault. The next two builds (`07287de`, `53bf2ac`) deployed automatically with no incident, so this session's manual `npx wrangler deploy` for `5e10f52` was a one-time recovery from an isolated platform hiccup, not evidence the integration needed reconnecting.
- Two earlier builds also show as failed in Build History — `f3efdaa` and `54ee016` (19–20 hours before this correction) — for an unrelated, already-diagnosed reason: `f3efdaa`'s deploy log reads `Invalid _redirects configuration: Maximum number of static _redirects rules limit of 2000 exceeded`, the exact D-147 ceiling breach. `c1cae30`, the very next build chronologically, is D-147's fix (2019/2000 breach → 1827/2000) and deployed cleanly, as has every build since. Nothing further to fix there.
- `2dca7c8` (this same KV-binding change) deployed automatically via the Git integration with no manual intervention — confirmed live: the `mb` Worker's Bindings tab shows all three bindings (`ASSETS`, `DB`, `ENQUIRY_RATE_LIMIT`) attached to the current production version, created at the time this build finished.

Net correction: the Git integration was never broken and does not need reconnecting or repair. Its two historical failures are now both explained — one already self-resolved by D-147, one a transient Cloudflare 503 — and `npx wrangler deploy` remains the correct fallback for exactly this kind of transient failure, not the normal deploy path.


## D-153 - AQA AS Level resources were rendering as "A LEVELS" everywhere resourceLevelLabel() is used

**Date:** 2026-09-08

**Trigger:** Owner's execution brief, workstream 4: "Fix AS Level resources displaying `A LEVELS`."

**What was actually wrong.** `resourceLevelLabel()` (`src/utils/content/collections.ts`) only knew about one AS/A signal: the `stage` field, built specifically for Cambridge 9701's combined "AS & A Level" syllabus (one qualification, split by topic depth). AQA's genuinely separate, standalone AS Level qualification (`qualifications: ["as-level"]`, `LEVEL_FOR_QUALIFICATION` bucketing it under `level: ["a-levels"]` — see that mapping's own comment in `src/utils/academic/index.ts`) is architecturally different: these resources correctly never set `stage`, because `validate-academic-content.mjs`'s stage-consistency check rejects `stage` on a resource whose syllabusTopics aren't themselves stage-tagged, which AQA's as-level taxonomy never is. `resourceLevelLabel` had no way to see this second AS signal at all, so all 4 of the site's AQA AS Level resources fell through to the generic branch and rendered "A LEVELS" — confirmed live on `/boards/aqa/as-level/business/` before the fix (resource cards under Study resources / Revision material / Exam preparation).

**What shipped:**
- `resourceLevelLabel()` now accepts an optional third argument, `qualifications`, and derives `effectiveStage = stage ?? (qualifications?.includes('as-level') ? 'AS' : undefined)`. The 9701 `stage` path is untouched; this only adds the second, independent AS signal.
- All 3 call sites updated to pass `entry.data.qualifications` / `d.qualifications`: `ResourceCard.astro`, `ResourcesSection.astro`, `resources/[slug].astro`.
- No content files were changed — the 4 AQA AS Level resource files correctly still have no `stage` field; the fix reads their existing `qualifications` field instead.
- New validator `scripts/validate-as-level-display.mjs`, wired into `validate:academic` (also `npm run validate:as-level-display` standalone): checks (1) `resourceLevelLabel`'s body still contains the `qualifications`-based derivation, (2) all 3 known call sites still pass 3 arguments, (3) every resource declaring `qualifications: ["as-level"]` also declares `level` including `"a-levels"` (the data precondition the fix depends on).

**Verification, including the negative case:** `node scripts/validate-as-level-display.mjs` passes. Negative-fixture proof: temporarily reverted `ResourceCard.astro`'s call to the old 2-argument form — validator FAILED with the exact expected message ("passes only 2 argument(s)"); file restored and re-verified passing. `npm run build` (2060 pages, 0 errors, `validate:academic` including this new check all green). `npx astro check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings (pre-existing 18 hints, unrelated). Checked the actual built output: `dist/boards/aqa/as-level/business/index.html` now contains 5 "AQA · AS LEVEL" resource-card labels (was 0 before the fix; genuine full A-Level resources on the same page still correctly show "AQA · A LEVELS", unaffected).

`node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs`: 35/36 passed. The one failure (`[Z]`) is a pre-existing, unrelated flake in that fixture's own restore step for a different validator (rendered-academic-label, IGCSE-corruption check) on a different file (`a-arenes-and-halogenoarenes-practice`) — it corrupted a `dist/` file to prove the validator catches it (that assertion passed) and then failed to restore that `dist/` output file afterward. `dist/` is gitignored (confirmed via `.gitignore` line 2 and `git status --short`, which shows nothing under `dist/` or referencing `arenes`) and is rebuilt from scratch by both `npm run build` locally and Cloudflare's own Workers Build on every deploy, so this has no bearing on the source tree or on production. Not investigated further under this entry since it is orthogonal to WS4; worth a look if it recurs.

**Not run this round:** `npm run audit:all`, `node scripts/test-cross-board-regression.mjs`, `npm audit`, and the functions/API unit tests were not re-run for this change — noted explicitly rather than silently assumed green. This change touches only resource-level display logic (one function signature, 3 call sites, 1 new validator) and does not touch pricing, commercial claims, the academic matrix, cross-board data, or the enquiry API, so the risk surface those suites cover is not implicated, but they have not been independently re-confirmed against this exact tree.


## D-154 - Duplicated assessment-component tier suffixes ("(Core) (Core)") fixed centrally; audit:rendered-labels' stale duplicate of resourceLevelLabel also fixed

**Date:** 2026-09-08

**Trigger:** Owner's execution brief, workstream 5: "Clean duplicated assessment labels such as `(Core) (Core)`."

**What was actually wrong.** `src/pages/boards/[board]/[qualification]/[subject].astro` (the one shared dynamic-route template for every board+qualification+subject hub page) renders each assessment component as `{comp.paperCode}: {comp.title}` followed unconditionally by a separate `({TIER_LABEL[comp.tier]})` badge whenever `comp.tier` is set. 18 of the 585 component titles in `src/data/academic/assessments.ts` already end in their own tier suffix as part of the genuine official component name (e.g. `'Non-calculator (Core)'`, `'Multiple Choice (Extended)'` -- 10 Core-suffixed, 8 Extended-suffixed; scanned programmatically, not estimated). For those 18, the page rendered `"Non-calculator (Core) (Core)"`. This is a single shared template, so the defect was present on every tiered syllabus hub across every board that had at least one such title -- not one syllabus page.

**What shipped:**
- The template's tier-badge span now only renders when `comp.title` does NOT already end with that same tier's parenthetical (`!comp.title.trim().endsWith(\`(${TIER_LABEL[comp.tier]})\`)`), so a title ending in a genuinely different parenthetical is unaffected and still gets its badge.
- `scripts/validate-rendered-academic-labels.mjs` (dist-dependent, wired into `audit:all` via `audit:rendered-labels`) gained a third check: scans every ACTIVE combination's built hub page for any immediately-repeated identical parenthetical after a component (`/\([A-Za-z][A-Za-z \-]*\)\s*\(\1\)/`), general enough to catch this bug class for any tier label (Higher/Foundation/etc.), not just Core/Extended.
- **Found and fixed in passing:** running this audit for WS5 immediately failed on 4 unrelated pages -- `audit:rendered-labels`' own `levelLabel()` helper (a hand-duplicated copy of `resourceLevelLabel`, by its own doc comment's admission a drift risk) was not updated when D-153 (WS4) added the `qualifications`-based AS derivation to the real function. Every AQA AS Level resource was rendering the now-correct `"AS LEVEL"` but failing this audit's stale expectation of `"A LEVELS"`. Fixed by updating the duplicate to match `resourceLevelLabel` exactly (same `qualifications` parameter, same derivation). This audit was not run as part of D-153 itself (noted there as "not run this round"); running it now for WS5 is what surfaced the gap.

**Verification, including the negative case:** `npm run build` (2060 pages) then `npm run audit:rendered-labels`: **1583 resource pages, 160 academic hub pages, and 160 assessment tables checked -- 0 problems**, covering every ACTIVE combination across Cambridge, AQA, OCR, Pearson Edexcel, OxfordAQA and IB, not a sample. Negative-fixture proof for the new check: backed up `dist/boards/cambridge/igcse/chemistry/index.html`, injected a duplicated `"(Core) (Core)"` into it directly, re-ran the audit -- FAILED with the exact expected message (`assessment component renders a duplicated tier suffix -- (Core) (Core)`) -- then restored the file byte-for-byte from the backup and re-ran clean. `npx astro check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings (same pre-existing 18 hints as D-153). `npx wrangler` deploy not run locally; ships via the Git integration confirmed healthy under D-152's correction.

**Not run this round:** `npm run audit:all`'s other 10 sub-checks, `node scripts/test-cross-board-regression.mjs`, `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs`, `npm audit`, and the functions/API unit tests were not re-run against this exact tree -- noted explicitly. This change touches only the shared assessment-table template and one dist-dependent audit script; it does not touch pricing, commercial claims, the matrix, cross-board data, or the enquiry API.

## D-155 - Alternative-paper assessment FAQs rewritten into explicit tier/alternative routes (Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 and 26 other tiered syllabuses)

**Date:** 2026-09-08

**Trigger:** Owner's execution brief, workstream 6: "Rewrite alternative-paper FAQs into explicit Core/Extended routes," naming Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 as the priority case, and explicitly instructing the routine to VERIFY against the current official syllabus first rather than trust existing sourcing.

**What was actually wrong.** The same shared template (`src/pages/boards/[board]/[qualification]/[subject].astro`) builds the "How is X assessed?" FAQ answer -- both the visible accordion and the JSON-LD FAQPage entry search engines and AI answer engines read independently -- by flattening every component of the primary assessment record into one semicolon-joined list, with no regard for `tier` or `alternativeGroup`. Live on `/boards/cambridge/igcse/chemistry/` before this fix, the answer read: *"Cambridge Chemistry (0620) is assessed through: Paper 1 (Multiple Choice (Core)) ...; Paper 3 (Theory (Core)) ...; Paper 2 (Multiple Choice (Extended)) ...; Paper 4 (Theory (Extended)) ...; Paper 5 (Practical Test) ...; Paper 6 (Alternative to Practical) ..."* -- wording indistinguishable from "sit all six papers," when a Core candidate actually sits Papers 1+3 and one of 5/6, and an Extended candidate sits Papers 2+4 and one of 5/6. Because this is the one shared template, the same ambiguity existed on every tiered syllabus's hub page across every board -- confirmed by a full scan of `src/data/academic/assessments.ts`: 163 `tier:` occurrences, 26 `alternativeGroup:` occurrences, 18 `routeGroup:` occurrences.

**Independent verification against the live official syllabus (done before touching code, per the brief's explicit instruction not to just trust existing sourcing):** fetched `https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/697205-2026-2028-syllabus.pdf` (the same URL already cited as `officialSourceUrl` on the 0620 record, `verifiedOn: '2026-08-26'`) live in this session on 2026-09-08. The PDF's "Assessment overview" section states verbatim: *"Core candidates take Paper 1 and Paper 3... Extended candidates take Paper 2 and Paper 4... All candidates take one practical paper from a choice of two: Paper 5... OR Paper 6..."*, with "candidates ... should be entered for Paper 1, Paper 3 and either Paper 5 or Paper 6" (Core) / "Paper 2, Paper 4 and either Paper 5 or Paper 6" (Extended). Every duration/marks/weighting in `assessments.ts` for 0620 matches the PDF exactly (Paper 1: 45 min/40 marks/30%; Paper 3: 1h15/80 marks/50%; Paper 2: 45 min/40 marks/30%; Paper 4: 1h15/80 marks/50%; Paper 5: 1h15/40 marks/20%; Paper 6: 1h/40 marks/20%). No discrepancy found between the official syllabus, the existing repo data, and the fix's output.

**What shipped:**
- The FAQ-generation block in the shared template now groups components by `tier` (using the existing `TIER_LABEL` vocabulary) when a syllabus has more than one tier, rendering `"<Tier> candidates take: <components>"` per tier, and renders any `alternativeGroup` members within a route as `"one of <A> or <B>"` rather than listing every alternative as though a candidate sits it. Untiered components shared across every route (e.g. 0620's Paper 5/6 choice, which belongs to neither tier) are included in each tier's route. Live output on `/boards/cambridge/igcse/chemistry/` after the fix: *"Core candidates take: Paper 1 (Multiple Choice (Core)) ...; Paper 3 (Theory (Core)) ...; one of Paper 5 (Practical Test) ... or Paper 6 (Alternative to Practical) .... Extended candidates take: Paper 2 (Multiple Choice (Extended)) ...; Paper 4 (Theory (Extended)) ...; one of Paper 5 ... or Paper 6 ...."*
- **Explicit scope decision, disclosed rather than silently absorbed:** `routeGroup`-style syllabuses (18 components site-wide, e.g. Cambridge IGCSE English Literature 0475's Drama-exam/Unseen/Coursework choices) are a genuinely different many-to-many composition model -- a single component can belong to several route groups simultaneously, unlike the one-tier-per-component model this fix handles. Building a correct describer for that model was judged out of scope for this pass; `routeGroup`-bearing assessments fall through unchanged to the pre-fix flat listing. Spot-checked `/boards/cambridge/igcse/english-literature/` after this fix and confirmed it renders exactly as before (flat list, not broken, not silently "fixed" incorrectly). Flagged here as a follow-up, not closed out.
- New regression guard: `scripts/validate-tiered-faq-routes.mjs`, wired into `audit:all` as `audit:tiered-faq-routes` (runs after `audit:rendered-labels`, same dist-dependent pattern). Two layers: (1) static -- confirms the template still contains the tier-grouping/alternativeGroup-aware generator code, catching a silent revert; (2) dynamic -- scans every built board/qualification/subject hub page's FAQ answer for any of five tier-label pairs (Core/Extended, Foundation/Higher, First Language/Second Language, AS/A2, SL/HL) appearing together without the "candidates take" route-grouping phrase, which is exactly the ambiguous pattern this fix eliminates. Deliberately data-driven -- does not hardcode which qualifications are tiered, so it keeps working as `assessments.ts` changes, and does not assert anything about `routeGroup` pages (the disclosed follow-up).

**Generalisation confirmed beyond 0620:** the fix is a single shared-template change, not a 0620-specific patch. A scan of the built `dist/boards/**` output found 27 hub pages now correctly tier-route-grouped across Cambridge (Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics, Physics), AQA (GCSE Biology/Chemistry/Mathematics/Physics), Edexcel (IGCSE Mathematics), and IB DP (Business, Economics, Environmental Systems & Societies, Geography, Global Politics, Language A: Language & Literature, and others) -- not sampled, the validator's own dynamic check counted all 159 hub pages with a "How is X assessed?" FAQ. Spot-checked AQA GCSE Chemistry (Foundation/Higher) and IB DP Economics (SL/HL) directly in the built HTML in addition to 0620 -- both render correctly route-grouped with the same "one of X or Y" alternative handling where applicable.

**Verification, including the negative case:** `npm run build` (2060 pages, `astro build` only -- `postbuild` pagefind indexing skipped as irrelevant to HTML-content checks, per the fast-iteration pattern established in D-153/D-154). First build surfaced 2 genuine TypeScript errors from the new code (`comp.tier`'s real type is `AssessmentTier | undefined`, not `string`, so the initial `(t): t is string` type-predicate was invalid) -- fixed by narrowing to `Exclude<NonNullable<...['tier']>, 'not-tiered'>` instead of a bare `string`; `npx astro check` then returned **0 errors, 0 warnings** (same 18 pre-existing hints as D-153/D-154, none new). `node scripts/validate-tiered-faq-routes.mjs` (via `npm run audit:tiered-faq-routes`): **0 problems**, 159 hub-page FAQ answers checked, 27 correctly tier-route-grouped. Negative-fixture proof, both layers: (1) dynamic -- stripped the "Core/Extended candidates take:" phrasing from the built 0620 page's FAQ text in place, re-ran the validator -- FAILED with the exact expected message naming the file and the ambiguous "(Core)"/"(Extended)" pair, then restored the file byte-for-byte and re-ran clean; (2) static -- renamed the `describeComponents` helper in the template source, re-ran the validator -- FAILED with the exact expected "missing expected WS6 logic" message, then restored the source byte-for-byte and re-ran clean.

**Not run this round:** `npm run audit:all`'s other sub-checks (only the new `audit:tiered-faq-routes` check was run standalone, not the full chain), `node scripts/test-cross-board-regression.mjs`, `node scripts/test-negative-validation-suite.mjs` (not extended to include the two new negative-fixture proofs above -- they were run as one-off scratch scripts, not added to the permanent suite), `npm audit`, and the functions/API unit tests were not re-run against this exact tree -- noted explicitly. This change touches only the shared assessment-FAQ-generation block in one template and adds one new dist-dependent audit script; it does not touch pricing, commercial claims, the matrix, cross-board integrity data, or the enquiry API. The `routeGroup` follow-up (18 components, e.g. 0475) remains open and is not claimed fixed by this entry.

## D-156 - IB DP Computer Science and Psychology modeled with matching dual current/future assessment records, closing both remaining subject gaps from D-129/D-138

**Date:** 2026-09-08

**Trigger:** Owner selected "Model a remaining subject gap" then "Both, one after another" (Computer Science and Psychology) as the next step after the GA4 BigQuery/practice-analytics workstream closed out this session.

**Starting state.** `syllabuses.ts` already carried entries for both subjects describing a legacy/current-vs-future transition in prose (Computer Science: 2014 course still active, 2027 course teaching since August 2025; Psychology: 2019 course still active, 2027 course teaching since August 2025), but neither syllabus's `code` field reflected the dual-course reality, and `assessments.ts` had exactly one record for each subject: Computer Science had none at all (a real `NOT_YET_MODELED` gap), and Psychology had a single record already renamed and reserved for the *future* 2027 course from an earlier session, leaving the *current*, presently-examined 2019 course with no assessment record of its own -- the syllabus students are actually sitting was the one without a modeled assessment table.

**Pattern followed.** The repo already has a proven precedent for this exact situation: OxfordAQA A-level Business, `syllabuses.ts` code `'9625 / 9725'`, with two `assessments.ts` records (`code: '9625'`, `specStatus: 'current'`, `relatedCode: '9725'`; and `code: '9725'`, `specStatus: 'future'`, `relatedCode: '9625'`). Both subjects here were modeled the same way.

**Computer Science.** `syllabuses.ts` code changed to `'DP Computer Science (2014) / DP Computer Science (2027)'`. New `assessments.ts` record added: `code: 'DP Computer Science (2014)'`, `specStatus: 'current'`, `relatedCode: 'DP Computer Science (2027)'`, `firstAssessment: '2014'`. Weighting/duration figures came directly from the IB's own official public subject briefs (Higher Level and Standard Level, both titled "First assessments 2014", fetched directly this session). Mark totals -- not published in either brief -- were independently confirmed against genuine IB markschemes fetched this session: HL Paper 1 (M23/4/COMSC/HP1) 100 marks (25+75); HL Paper 2 (M19/4/COMSC/HP2) 65 marks (stated verbatim "Total 65 marks"); HL Paper 3 (M19/4/COMSC/HP3) 30 marks (4+8+6+12, stated verbatim "Total: [30]"); SL Paper 1 (M19/4/COMSC/SP1) 70 marks (25+45); SL Paper 2 (M19/4/COMSC/SP2) 45 marks (stated verbatim). Internal Assessment (a computational solution for a real client) marked against five criteria -- Planning 6, Solution Overview 6, Development 12, Functionality and Extensibility 4, Evaluation 6 -- 34 marks total at both tiers, corroborated across an independent school library research guide (itself citing the official 2012 IB guide) plus a second independent summary agreeing on both total and per-criterion split. The future (2027) course's own assessment record remains explicitly out of scope for this round -- its curriculum structure is registered in `syllabuses.ts` but no published paper-by-paper mark breakdown was located (it has not yet been examined; no specimen papers with mark totals exist yet). This is disclosed in the new record's `internalNotes`, not silently absorbed.

**Psychology.** `syllabuses.ts` code changed to `'DP Psychology (2019) / DP Psychology (2027)'`. The existing (future, 2027) `assessments.ts` record's `code` field and cross-reference were confirmed already correct from a prior session; its `notes`/`internalNotes` were updated to point at the new sibling record and mark the previously-flagged Paper 1/Paper 3 mark-total gap as closed. New `assessments.ts` record added: `code: 'DP Psychology (2019)'`, `specStatus: 'current'`, `relatedCode: 'DP Psychology (2027)'`, `firstAssessment: '2019'`. Mark totals verified against genuine IB markschemes: Paper 1 (M19/3/PSYCH/SP1) 49 marks; Paper 3 (M19/3/PSYCH/HP3) 24 marks; Paper 2 SL/HL totals (22/44) carried over from a prior session's sourcing. Internal Assessment: 22 marks across 4 criteria (Introduction 6, Exploration 4, Analysis 6, Evaluation 6). **A genuine sourcing discrepancy was found and resolved, and the resolution is documented in the record's `notes` rather than silently picking a number:** one source (a PDF titled "IB PSYCHOLOGY HL Internal Assessment Criteria") listed 9 criteria (A-I) summing to 34 marks, conflicting with multiple other sources stating 22 marks across 4 criteria. Resolved by fetching a directly-dated (May 2019) primary account naming the exact 4 criteria matching this syllabus era, concluding the 34-mark/9-criteria document describes an older, already-superseded pre-2019 revision; the 22-mark breakdown was independently cross-verified against the subject brief's own stated IA weighting (25% SL / 20% HL).

**Sourcing method used throughout:** official IB subject briefs for weighting/duration/structure (never disputed), cross-checked against genuine primary IB markschemes (identifiable by exam-code headers, e.g. `M23/4/COMSC/HP1/ENG/TZ1/XX/M`, and IB copyright notices) mirrored on `papacambridge.com` and `xtremepape.rs` for mark totals not published in the briefs themselves -- consistent with this repo's established I07/D-129 policy of accepting authentic mirrors of real board documents regardless of hosting domain, provided `officialSourceUrl` still points at the board's own official page.

**Verification.** `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/validate-assessments.mjs`: **PASSED**, 166 records, all 14 structural rules clean, including rule 6 (exactly one `current` record per board+qualification+subject+tier-overlap group) and rule 11 (`future` records genuinely later-dated than their `current`/`legacy-teach-out` siblings). Full `npm run validate:academic` gate run: matrix, content tagging, commercial claims, cross-board integrity, pricing consistency, review integrity, pinned teachers, worker bindings, AS-level display, FX policy, assessments, and grade thresholds all **PASSED**. One real defect was caught and fixed by this gate: `syllabus-topics.ts`'s existing Computer Science (2027-only) topic collection still declared the old bare `syllabusCode: 'DP Computer Science'`, which no longer matched `syllabuses.ts`'s new compound code -- cross-board-integrity rule [1] failed with exactly the intended message, confirming the check works; fixed by updating the topic collection's `syllabusCode` to the compound string, re-ran clean. `validate-practice-question-schema.mjs` could not be run in this environment (missing `node_modules`/`astro` dependency, unrelated to this change -- a pre-existing sandbox limitation, not a new failure introduced here).

**Not run this round:** `npm run build`/`astro check` (no dependency install available in this sandbox), `audit:all`'s dist-dependent sub-checks, `test-cross-board-regression.mjs`, `test-negative-validation-suite.mjs`, `npm audit`, and the functions/API unit tests. ## D-158 - WS7: first weekly GSC-driven optimization batch, sourced via Supermetrics (owner connected it this session)

**Date:** 2026-09-08

**Trigger:** Owner's execution brief, workstream 7: "Run weekly GSC-driven optimization batches of only 5-10 URLs." The owner's own answer to this session's earlier clarifying question was "not sure / check Supermetrics" for GSC access; the owner then connected the Supermetrics connector and authenticated its Google Search Console data source (`sc-domain:marlbridge.com`) mid-session, at my request, via two separate steps (connector-level OAuth, then a second Supermetrics-internal login for the GSC data source specifically).

**What already existed, discovered before building anything new:** `docs/growth/README.md` documents a mature, already-built Search Console demand engine with two ingestion paths that both feed the same canonical scoring function (`scripts/growth/scoring.mjs`'s `classifyQuery`, deliberately extracted so neither path forks the analysis logic): (1) a CSV-import path (`npm run growth:gsc`, run once before against a real owner-supplied export, 2 Sep 2026) and (2) a live path (`functions/_lib/gsc-refresh.ts`, Cron-triggered daily plus a manual "Refresh now" button on `/admin/search-demand/`) that pulls from the real Search Console API into a Cloudflare D1 database, per D-125. Confirmed via `validate-worker-bindings.mjs`'s output that `GSC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` is a known, declared secret -- the live path's credentials are configured and it should be running daily. **Not verified this round:** the live D1 dashboard's actual current contents, or reconciling its numbers against this week's Supermetrics-sourced snapshot below. Both paths exist; this entry only exercises the CSV path, freshly fed by Supermetrics instead of a manual export, which is exactly the "connector path (Supermetrics, if the owner authorizes it)" the README's own architecture note anticipated without committing to before authorization existed.

**What was done:**
1. Queried Supermetrics' Google Search Console connector directly (`data_query` against `ds_id: GW`, `sc-domain:marlbridge.com`) for the last 28 days: queries with >=10 impressions (94 rows) and pages with >=20 impressions (110 rows) -- filtered at query time to keep the pull a manageable size, not because lower-traffic rows are unimportant; the full unfiltered query pull (no impression floor) was seen once inline before filtering and showed a long tail of hundreds of 0-1-impression queries that cannot mathematically qualify for any of `classifyQuery`'s opportunity types (all require >=15-20 impressions).
2. Converted this into the exact CSV shape (`Top queries`/`Top pages`, `Clicks`, `Impressions`, `CTR` as a percentage string, `Position`) Search Console's own UI export produces, saved to `.growth-private/exports/2026-09-08/` (gitignored, not committed, per this directory's own established policy).
3. Ran the existing, unmodified `npm run growth:gsc -- --input .growth-private/exports/2026-09-08 --out .growth-private/reports/gsc-opportunity-report-2026-09-08.md` -- zero changes to the scoring script itself, reusing the exact tested pipeline.

**Result of the query-level scoring:** 101 queries classified -- 14 `EMERGING_DEMAND`, 2 `CTR_OPPORTUNITY`, 85 `LOW_PRIORITY`. **Zero `QUICK_WIN` or `NEAR_PAGE_ONE` queries** (the position 4-20 bands) in this window -- consistent with the 2 Sep report's own finding that the site is still building initial ranking authority. No flagship-code (0620/0625/0580/9701/9702) query demand visible either. Per this programme's own stated priority order ("a decision not to change a page is valid when evidence doesn't support changing it"), the query-level data alone did not support a batch this week.

**How the actual 8-URL batch was derived instead:** `scripts/growth/gsc-opportunity-report.mjs` only classifies queries, not pages -- WS7 asks for URLs. Applied the identical, already-documented `CTR_OPPORTUNITY` rule from `scripts/growth/scoring.mjs` (expected-CTR floor by position band: 10% for position <=3, 3% for position <=10, 1% otherwise; impressions >= 50 threshold) to the page-level report instead of inventing a new rule. This surfaced 8 URLs that already rank on page one (position ~7.0-10.0) but are earning far less click-through than that position should produce -- a real, reproducible, deterministic signal, not a judgment call:

| URL | Position | CTR | Impressions |
|---|---|---|---|
| /boards/cambridge/o-level/statistics/ | 7.0 | 0.55% | 181 |
| /resources/o-level-islamiyat-paper-1-revision-notes/ | 10.0 | 0.87% | 115 |
| /resources/o-level-pakistan-studies-land-of-pakistan/ | 8.3 | 1.30% | 77 |
| /resources/igcse-english-literature-paper-4-unseen/ | 8.2 | 2.20% | 91 |
| /resources/igcse-cambridge-islamiyat-paper-2/ | 7.9 | 1.72% | 58 |
| /resources/a-level-economics-price-system-and-the-microeconomy/ | 7.2 | 1.79% | 56 |
| /resources/a-level-cambridge-ict-hardware-and-software/ | 7.1 | 1.85% | 54 |
| /resources/igcse-english-literature-paper-1-poetry-and-prose-revision-notes/ | 8.2 | 2.70% | 74 |

**Editorial action taken on 7 of the 8 (title/meta-description CTR tuning, not content rewriting):** the first URL, `/boards/cambridge/o-level/statistics/`, is rendered by the shared `[board]/[qualification]/[subject].astro` template, whose title and meta description are entirely formula-computed from board/qualification/subject/syllabus-code/resource-count data (a deliberate design from the Aug 2026 SEO remediation, Section 227 comment in that file) -- there is no per-page override, so a single-page fix would mean changing the shared formula for all 160 hub pages, which is out of this entry's scope and not attempted. Left as an open, disclosed item, not silently dropped.

The other 7 are resource pages, which do carry a real per-page override mechanism: `d.seoTitle ?? d.title` and `d.seoDescription ?? d.description` in `src/pages/resources/[slug].astro`, backed by a Zod schema (`src/content.config.ts`) requiring `seoTitle` <=60 chars and `seoDescription` 70-160 chars. None of the 7 had ever set these fields, so they were falling back to their long, accurate, but snippet-unfriendly on-page `description` (up to 370 characters) -- the site's own `metaDescription()` helper (`src/utils/seo/meta.ts`) already truncates anything over 165 chars at a word boundary for the actual meta/og/twitter tags, so the live problem was not raw truncation breaking the page, but that the auto-truncated preview reads as an abruptly-cut sentence fragment rather than a complete, compelling one.

Added `seoDescription` to all 7 (each a shorter, complete, accurate paraphrase of the existing on-page `description` -- no new facts, no fabrication, verified against the source description word-for-word before writing) and `seoTitle` to 1 of the 7 (`igcse-cambridge-islamiyat-paper-2`, whose original title "Cambridge IGCSE Islamiyat: Paper 2 (0493)" didn't signal it was a study guide). This is title/meta tuning only -- no resource body content, word count, or structure was touched, consistent with the brief's explicit "do NOT optimize for word count" instruction.

**Verification, including the negative case:** ran the full `validate:academic` chain (14 validators, all passed, including the Zod-schema-adjacent `validate-academic-content.mjs`) then a full `astro build` (2060 pages, ~1m49s) -- 0 build errors. Read the actual rendered `<title>` and `<meta name="description">` out of all 7 built HTML files and confirmed each matches the authored `seoTitle`/`seoDescription` exactly (not truncated, since all were authored within the schema's own 60/160-char limits). `npx astro check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings (same 18 pre-existing hints as D-153 through D-155, none new). Did not re-run `npm run audit:all` or the negative-fixture suite this round -- this change touches only frontmatter metadata on 7 files, not template logic, so no new validator was warranted (unlike D-153/D-154/D-155, which changed shared rendering logic).

**Not run this round:** reconciling the live D1 `/admin/search-demand/` dashboard's own data against this week's Supermetrics snapshot (flagged above); GA4 data (still not connected in this session); setting up any kind of automated weekly cadence (e.g. a scheduled task) for future batches -- this entry is one manually-run week, not an automation, and starting a recurring job wasn't something the owner was asked about yet. The Pages.csv export was itself truncated to the top ~110 pages by the order Supermetrics returned them in (not explicitly sorted) to keep the pull a manageable size for this session -- not a complete page-level census, disclosed rather than presented as exhaustive.

**Owner follow-up:** none required to consider this week's batch complete -- but future weeks need either a repeat of this same manual Supermetrics pull, or a decision to rely on the already-running live D1 path instead (worth checking what it actually shows first, since it may already have a longer, more complete trend history than any single 28-day snapshot).

## D-159 - 19 missing IB DP/MYP + OCR/OxfordAQA A-Level Chemistry topic taxonomies added to `syllabus-topics.ts`, closing the D-137-disclosed gap

**Date:** 2026-09-08

**Trigger:** D-137 disclosed that DP Chemistry's `syllabus-topics.ts` entry (and several sibling subjects) had genuine but incomplete `syllabusTopics` coverage, leaving affected resources falling back to syllabus-wide tagging instead of precise topic tagging. Re-scoping this against the current `matrix.ts` (which has grown since D-137) found 19 board+qualification+subject combinations with an ACTIVE matrix entry, a real assessment record, and a real `syllabuses.ts` record, but no `syllabus-topics.ts` topic collection at all: 11 IB DP subjects (Biology, Business Management, Environmental Systems and Societies, Geography, Global Politics, World History, Language A: Language and Literature, Language A: Literature, Language B, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation), 1 further IB DP subject researched alongside them for completeness (Psychology, whose existing entry had been assumed present but was not), 5 IB MYP subjects (Sciences, Mathematics, Design, Individuals and Societies, Language Acquisition), and 2 UK-board A-Level Chemistry specifications (OCR H432, OxfordAQA 9620).

**Sourcing method.** Each subject was researched independently (18 of the 19 via separate agent dispatches, each given the exact schema, a real template example, the specific official source URL, subject-specific structural hints to verify rather than trust, and an explicit no-fabrication instruction; Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation was sourced directly from the official guide's full text, already fetched and saved from an earlier session pass, rather than re-dispatching an agent). Every topic/subtopic name and number traces to an official source actually fetched and read -- IB subject briefs/guides, or the OCR/OxfordAQA specification PDFs -- never invented or guessed to fill the schema. Several genuine sourcing obstacles were hit and resolved without compromising the no-fabrication rule:
- Two dead/blocked official URLs recovered via Wayback Machine captures verified through the CDX API as genuine 200/`application/pdf` archival crawls (MYP Mathematics, MYP Sciences), one recovered via a byte-identical school-hosted mirror of the same official PDF (MYP Design) after a live-browser pass confirmed the mirror's first page matched word-for-word.
- Multiple Cloudflare bot-checks on ibo.org required either a rendered browser session or a Wayback capture instead of a direct fetch.
- Where IB's own DP subject guides give no official numbered sub-content (Global Politics, both Language A courses, Language B, Psychology) or where an entire programme (MYP) has no numbered content syllabus at all (schools design their own units around key/related concepts, global contexts and lettered assessment criteria), `subtopics` was left as `[]` throughout rather than inventing decimal numbering -- consistent with this file's existing convention (see D-137, and the already-shipped Chemistry/Computer Science/Global Politics entries).
- One genuine internal inconsistency was found and preserved, not silently reconciled: the MYP Mathematics subject brief names "four branches of mathematical study" as (1) Numerical and abstract reasoning, (2) Thinking with models, (3) Spatial reasoning, (4) Reasoning with data in its Section I overview, but separately, under Criterion A, describes a *different* four-branch list (number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability) that the document never reconciles. Both are quoted in that entry's `notes`; only the explicitly-numbered Section I list was used to populate `subtopics`.
- One finding flagged for future review rather than acted on unilaterally: independent web searches (not the IB subject brief itself) suggested the DP Psychology 2019-generation syllabus may have already run its final standard examination session in May 2026, which would make it `superseded` rather than `current`. This was not corroborated against an authoritative IB source during this pass, so the new `syllabus-topics.ts` entry keeps `status: 'current'` to match the existing, more directly IB-sourced `syllabuses.ts` record (which itself states this is "the one current DP cohorts are actually examined under today", verified 2026-09-08) -- the discrepancy is disclosed in the entry's `notes` for a future pass to re-verify directly against IB's own curriculum-updates page.

**Splice mechanics.** Learning from the anchor-collision bug in an earlier session's `assessments.ts` edit, each of the 19 entries was drafted as a standalone file, then spliced into `SYLLABUS_VERSIONS` programmatically (a small Python script) using the array's own unique closing anchor (`] as const;`, confirmed to occur exactly once in the file, immediately followed by the `KNOWN_OTHER_SERIES` export) rather than a hand-edited insertion point -- eliminating the class of bug that corrupted an unrelated record last time.

**Validation problems found and fixed (working as designed):**
1. `validate-cross-board-integrity.mjs` rule [2] failed: the new Global Politics entry's `sourceUrl` used the bare host `ibo.org` instead of the board's verified domain `www.ibo.org`. Fixed.
2. Rule [1] failed: the new Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation entry's `syllabusCode` used lowercase "applications and interpretation" where `syllabuses.ts`'s verified code capitalizes it ("Applications and Interpretation"). Fixed to match exactly.
3. Rule [1] failed: the new Psychology entry's `syllabusCode` was the bare `'DP Psychology'`, but `syllabuses.ts`'s verified code for this subject is the compound `'DP Psychology (2019) / DP Psychology (2027)'` (IB runs two syllabus generations side by side, per the existing `syllabuses.ts` record) -- the same class of fix D-156 already made for Computer Science. Fixed.

All three were the validator correctly catching real inconsistencies, not false positives.
